name: Renderer separation: RealityKit + WebKit as siloed, simplified frameworks
description:
## Why
Both renderers must live side by side behind a developer switch, each in its own extension-safe framework over a renderer-neutral core, so either can be tested, swapped or deleted by removing one target. The move is also the chance to make both smaller and spec-correct.

Supersedes the ordering of 0x5lhruu (delete RealityKit): nothing is deleted until the renderer decision; then the losing framework and the switch go.

## Sources
- Plan (authoritative): .agents/plans/2026-09-30-renderer-separation.md
- Research: .agents/research/2026-09-30-renderer-separation-assumptions.md, -realitykit-renderer-best-practices.md, -webkit-renderer-best-practices.md, -rendering-validity-and-testing.md

## Decisions taken (user: "go with your recommendations", 2026-09-30)
- Yaw 0 = Khronos default view; web goldens regenerated once.
- RealityKit keeps the system tone map; the gap is declared as a RendererFeature.
- Policy defaults (Sketchfab BLEND fixes, baked-emissive drop, -2 EV with file lights) kept, moved into a reported Policy step.
- Core owns shared value types; PreviewUI is never linked into appexes.

## Scope
Branch renderer-separation in .worktrees/renderer-separation (from webkit-renderer + its uncommitted snapshot, then main merged). Seams 1-11 of the plan.

## Done when
The plan's "Done when" list holds.

## Verification
The plan's Verification block, per renderer switch value.
result: All 11 seams done on branch renderer-separation (.worktrees/renderer-separation, head 1b786a5). GLTFCore + RendererRealityKit + RendererWebKit extension-safe frameworks; Shared/ gone; hidden renderer switch (Debug Develop menu, RealityKit default) drives window/QL/thumbnail; either renderer removable with zero code edits (tests pass). Both renderers simplified (RK -1147 LOC, WebKit -363 LOC) with pinned per-renderer goldens. Not merged to main; renderer decision still open.

name: EXP-009: cutout-as-mask for factor-1 BLEND
description:
## Classification
NEW

## Hypothesis
I believe 81 factor-1 BLEND foliage primitives on vegetation_pack each build an uncached full-res opacity TextureResource; treating detected cutout like native MASK (threshold only) deletes that work without quality loss vs current 0.4 cutoff.

## Parent champion
EXP-006-v2

## Research basis
Profiler: vegetation 8287ms vs cinema 1214ms at similar tris; 81/93 BLEND factor-A=1; opacityTexture not in texture cache.

## Scope / forbidden
- Do not skip textures entirely
- Do not change cinema/opaque paths
- Same-machine control; require 07-isolated win (08 must not move equally)
- Search WHAT-WE-TRIED first

## Approach
In RealityKitConvert+Material applyBlendMode, when alphaUsage==.cutout and factor≈1, set opacityThreshold like MASK and skip opacityTexture.

## Done when
Full 10-GLB bench + control; KEEP|REJECT|INCONCLUSIVE; ledger updated
result:
## Decision
KEEP

## Hypothesis
Factor-1 BLEND + detected cutout was building uncached full-res opacity TextureResources; MASK-like threshold-only deletes that work.

## What changed
`RealityKitConvert+Material.swift` — detected cutout sets opacityThreshold=0.4 only (no opacityTexture). Merged to champion.

## Evidence
- Candidate: 7732.9 ms sum_median_total
- Same-machine champ: 14677.8
- Isolated: −6944.9 ms (−47.3%)
- 07-vegetation: −6744 ms (−89%); 08-cinema: −1 ms (flat)

## Correctness
0/10 errors; threshold-only cutout vs prior opacity map (same 0.4)

## Complexity
tiny (−5/+2 one file)

## Artifacts
experiments/results/EXP-009.json, EXP-009-champ.json; branch exp/009-cutout-as-mask@90def67

## Must not retry
Re-adding opacityTexture for detected cutout without a new fidelity-gated hypothesis.

name: EXP-012: Early-out / single-pass UV wrap+flip
description:
## Rank
3

## Classification
VARIANT (of deleted pre-009 orchestrator-invented “UV wrap” queue — recreated only with citations)

## Hypothesis
I believe `bakedTextureCoordinates` always unpacks UVs, runs `TextureUV.wrapSingleTile` (full min/max scan + optional remap), then a second full `map` for RealityKit V-flip — paying O(verts) twice (or thrice) on high-poly assets whose UVs already lie in a single unit tile (06-stone, 07-vegetation, 08-cinema dominate vertex counts). A cheap unit-square early-out and/or single-pass wrap+flip should shrink residual mesh convert without changing sampler wrap semantics for true multi-tile / transform cases.

## Parent champion
EXP-011

## Research basis (links)
- Local: `Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift` `bakedTextureCoordinates` — unpack → wrapSingleTile → V-flip map.
- Local: `Shared/TextureUV.swift` — UDIM tile bake; early return when tile==.zero after full min/max.
- Khronos glTF 2.0 samplers wrapS/wrapT.
- Corpus vertex pressure: stone/vegetation/cinema.

## Approach (one change)
Optimize only the UV bake path: early-out and/or fuse wrap-tile + V-flip. Do not delete UDIM correction; do not change KHR_texture_transform; do not disable sampler address modes.

## Likely files
- Shared/TextureUV.swift
- Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift

## Done when
- Bench vs same-machine EXP-011 control; wins on high-vert assets without UDIM regressions.
- KEEP/REJECT per PROTOCOL.

## Forbidden / out of scope
- Removing wrap / broken UVs; special-casing corpus; texture/material changes; parallel benches; champion merge
result:
## Decision
REJECT

## Hypothesis / Change / Batch
Fuse wrapSingleTile + RealityKit V-flip into one in-place pass (wrapSingleTileAndFlipV). Parent champion EXP-011 @ 1329a23. Commit 09cef9b (not kept).

## Champion control / Candidate / Delta
Control EXP-012-champ: 7534.1 ms
Candidate EXP-012: 7684.1 ms
Delta: +150.0 ms (+1.99%) — within 3% noise (~226 ms of control / ~240 ms of ledger 8002); wrong direction.

## Per-asset / Correctness / Complexity / Reason / Must not retry
06-stone +32.1, 07-vegetation +57.4, 08-cinema +44.9 (hypothesized wins inverted). 2/10 faster (02, 10). 0/10 load errors; TextureUVTests 5/5 (fuse≡separate). Complexity low (+52/−2).
Reason: UV bake residual not measurable after EXP-011; fused pass does not help.
Must not retry: same fused wrap+V-flip without evidence UV bake dominates residual.

## Worktree / SHA
Removed .worktrees/exp-012 and branch exp/EXP-012. SHA was 09cef9b (discarded).

name: Read-model adapters (SceneModel, Availability, Playback)
description:
## Scope
Value/read side. See parent `mhapkvgf` for shared context, seam file paths, and the fixture test table.

- **`EngineSceneModel` (struct, Sendable)** over `GLTFSessionDocument` + `PreviewStats` + `ModelDimensions` + `GLTFValidationState` + `PipelineReport`:
  - Build `nodeTree` from flat `document.nodes` child indices; radians→degrees for camera fov / light cones.
  - Materials already carry `workflow`/`alphaMode`/`isDoubleSided` + factors + bound `materialIndices` (g21akn5r). `materialVariantNames` from the host variant list.
  - **Validation is async** (nil while pending; `.success`/`.failed`/`.skipped` after first paint): rebuild the struct when it resolves; map `.failed`/`.skipped` to a synthetic info `ValidationResult.Issue`, never silence.
- **`Availability`** via `DerivedAvailability<EngineSceneModel>` (already written), fed channels from `EntityLoader.LoadedModel.debugModes` (`EntityLoader.swift:11`). Do **not** persist raw JSON on the document.
- **`AnimationPlaybackController`** (`@MainActor @Observable final class`) over the `PreviewScene` clock + `PreviewClip`; read exact members in `PreviewUI/Seam/AnimationPlaybackController.swift`. The RealityKit clock may no-op `advance`.

## Tests (via `GLBPreviewTests/TestFixtures.swift`)
`.cube`/`.tiny`→plain; `.boxAnimated`→`hasAnimations`+clips; `.lights`→`hasLights`; `.cameras`→`hasCameras`; `.multiScene`→`isMultiScene`; `.rigged`→`hasSkin`; `.morph`→`hasMorphs`; `.missingChannels`→shorter `availableDebugChannels`; `.invalid`→validation issues; `.offcenter`→`authoredOrigin != .zero`.

## Done when
Read adapters + tests green. No PreviewUI rewrites; no engine changes.

name: Renderer: second renderer that shares a loaded scene
description:
**Why:** the inspector preview must not load the file twice (GPU memory, load time).

**Scope:** `MetalRenderer`: `public init(sharing scene: MetalScene, device:)` or `func adopt(_ scene: MetalScene)` that sets `scene`, rebuilds `drawLists`, keeps its own `pipelines`, `materialResources`, `drawVisibility`; `MetalEnvironment.shared` is already shared. Must use the same `MTLDevice` as the scene's buffers (`scene.draws[0].vertexBuffer.device`). `ModelView`: `public func show(scene: MetalScene, options: ViewOptions)` path that adopts instead of loading a URL (fit + redraw as `load` does). `ModelCanvasController`: `public private(set) var sceneGeneration: Int` bumped on every successful load/reload, and `public var scene: MetalScene?` (the view's `renderer.scene`) so another view can adopt it.

**Done when:** a second `ModelView` shows a model loaded by the first without reading the file; after the first reloads (scene/variant change) the second can re-adopt.
**Verification:** unit test: adopt → same `MTLBuffer` identities (`===`) as the source scene, image renders non-empty; `./scripts/dev.sh test`.

**Spec:** `.agents/plans/2026-11-04-scene-interaction.md` (coverage table + decisions log). Read `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md` first.
**Rules:** work on `main` unless told otherwise; never regenerate pixel references for a default render (`TestModels/References/`); new UI goes through `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/` components; check UI on screen yourself (`./scripts/dev.sh run <fixture>`, `screencapture`), never ask the user to test.

## TDD execution contract
- The cases below are defined test contracts, not implemented tests or observed failures. Baseline: **not run for this backlog edit**. Use existing suites where they cover the behavior; proposed suite names are destinations, not existing files.
- **Red first:** after prerequisites are available, add the smallest deterministic behavioral test before its production change. Run the focused suite and record test name, command, revision/worktree state, actual failing assertion and log path. A missing API/compiler error may guide initial scaffolding, but establish a compiling behavioral failure before implementation; build/tool/fixture errors are not feature-red evidence. Never use unconditional failures, skip/expected-failure markers, or loosen an oracle to manufacture red.
- **Green, then refactor:** implement only enough to pass that test, run the remaining cases, then refactor with tests green. Blocked leaves define tests now and establish executable red after their prerequisite lands; do not invent placeholder dependencies.
- For already implemented behavior, keep the regression green and, where safe, prove sensitivity using a temporary isolated mutation/reversion of only that behavior. Do not undo another worker's edits or claim retroactive red. Record unavailable red evidence honestly.
- **Completion evidence:** case → test/fixture → observed red (or documented existing-behavior exception) → green, with commands and log paths in the result. Passing tests alone do not prove this contract was followed.

### Defined tests (write before production changes)
1. Adopt a two-mesh scene: source and preview share identical vertex/index MTLBuffer objects; a loader spy records no second file read.
2. Reload the source, re-adopt its new scene generation, and render the new geometry; source visibility, camera and material state stay independent.
3. Render both views offscreen: both contain expected geometry; disposing one leaves the other usable.

### TDD verification
Focused command: `./scripts/dev.sh test -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/SharedSceneTests` (reuse/extend an existing suite if appropriate; confirm tests are discovered and executed, not zero tests). After green run `./scripts/dev.sh test` including unchanged pixel references. Use hand-computed expectations/independent Khronos output for renderer math, not values copied from the implementation.

For UI assertions prefer deterministic in-process hosted components and background AX selection; visual checks must inspect the actual rendered result. These instructions supersede older generic launch/uitest directions in this description: background only, no focus steal, no `--snapshot`, no leftover Export sheets; XCUITest requires explicit approval for that run. No app launch is required for this backlog edit.

No adopt/shared-scene entry point or sceneGeneration exists yet. First introduce the agreed callable interface, then implement the defined buffer-identity/load-spy tests and observe compiling behavioral red before the adoption algorithm. No placeholder loader is added here.

Do not label this leaf test-ready until its defined cases compile, execute and fail on behavior. Interface/build errors are not feature-red evidence.

name: EXP-003: Lane C QL host reuse / overlap
description:

## Scope
- One change: reuse a host in the QL extension, start the page before the file is applied, or unhide after load without extra look commands
- Isolated worktree `.worktrees/wk-fp-003`
- Out of scope: KTX/Draco defer, IBL content, bench format

## Done when
- One `perf:` commit in the experiment worktree
- Smoke build succeeded
- Parent benches KEEP/REJECT

## Verification
Parent runs `./scripts/webkit-first-paint-bench.sh --label EXP-003`. KEEP: ≥12% proc-cold visibleMs on BoomBox and Corset. A QL-only reuse win that the still-bench cannot see must be called out with a second measurement (warm vs new host in-process is acceptable evidence).

Ledger: `.worktrees/webkit-renderer/docs/webkit-first-paint-experiments.md`

name: Navigation gizmo: live axis balls that orbit with the camera
description:
**Why:** the bottom-leading `GLTFInspector/Canvas/OrientationGizmo.swift` is a fixed isometric triad; it does not follow the camera, so it does not tell you which way you are looking. Replace it with a proper navigation gizmo like Blender/design tools: the user supplied reference screenshots (2026-11-04).

**Target look (from the user's screenshots):**
```
 ┌──────────────┐   rounded-square dark panel (glass/HUD tone), ~72–80 pt
 │      ● Y     │   positive axes: filled balls in DS.Color.Axis.x/y/z (red/green/blue)
 │  ●   │   ●   │   negative axes: smaller muted grey balls on the opposite side
 │   ╲  │  ╱    │   thin lines from the centre to each positive ball in the axis colour
 │ ●────┼────●  │   (lines to negative balls in muted grey)
 │      ●       │   balls depth-sorted: farther ones drawn first and slightly dimmer
 └──────────────┘   looking straight down an axis: that ball sits in the centre, on top
```

**Scope:**
- Renderer: expose the live view rotation. `ModelView` publishes `public var onOrientation: ((simd_float3x3) -> Void)?` (rotation part of the current view matrix; for a file camera use its view matrix) whenever it redraws; `ModelCanvasController` forwards it to an observable `public private(set) var viewRotation: simd_float3x3` (throttle to changes only).
- App: new `GLTFInspector/Canvas/NavigationGizmo.swift` (replace `OrientationGizmo` at the same place in `CanvasRegion.swift`). Project the six unit axes with `viewRotation`, draw with SwiftUI `Canvas`, sort by view-space z. Panel via a DesignSystem component (add `DSGizmoPanel` or reuse `DSHUDCapsule`/glass tokens in `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/`) — no hard-coded colours outside `DS`.
- Interaction: hover highlights a ball; click a ball snaps the orbit camera to look down that axis (map ±X/±Y/±Z to `CameraPreset` right/left/top/bottom/front/back via `ViewState.show(_:)`); click the already-front ball flips to the opposite view; drag inside the panel orbits the camera (forward to the same orbit as a canvas drag via a new `ModelCanvasController.orbit(dx:dy:)`).
- Accessibility: one element "Navigation gizmo" with actions per view ("View from top", …).

**Out:** gizmo for file-camera editing; roll.
**Done when:** orbiting the model rotates the gizmo live in sync; Front view shows Z ball centred toward the viewer like the second screenshot's centred ball; clicking each ball shows the matching view; dragging on the gizmo orbits; looks like the screenshots in light and dark appearance.
**Verification:** unit test for the projection + depth sort (pure function: rotation → ordered ball positions) and ball → preset mapping; `./scripts/dev.sh run cube`, screenshots at front/top/isometric next to the reference look; `./scripts/dev.sh test`.

**Spec:** `.agents/plans/2026-11-04-scene-interaction.md` (coverage table + decisions log). Read `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md` first.
**Rules:** work on `main` unless told otherwise; never regenerate pixel references for a default render (`TestModels/References/`); new UI goes through `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/` components; check UI on screen yourself (`./scripts/dev.sh run <fixture>`, `screencapture`), never ask the user to test.

## TDD execution contract
- The cases below are defined test contracts, not implemented tests or observed failures. Baseline: **not run for this backlog edit**. Use existing suites where they cover the behavior; proposed suite names are destinations, not existing files.
- **Red first:** after prerequisites are available, add the smallest deterministic behavioral test before its production change. Run the focused suite and record test name, command, revision/worktree state, actual failing assertion and log path. A missing API/compiler error may guide initial scaffolding, but establish a compiling behavioral failure before implementation; build/tool/fixture errors are not feature-red evidence. Never use unconditional failures, skip/expected-failure markers, or loosen an oracle to manufacture red.
- **Green, then refactor:** implement only enough to pass that test, run the remaining cases, then refactor with tests green. Blocked leaves define tests now and establish executable red after their prerequisite lands; do not invent placeholder dependencies.
- For already implemented behavior, keep the regression green and, where safe, prove sensitivity using a temporary isolated mutation/reversion of only that behavior. Do not undo another worker's edits or claim retroactive red. Record unavailable red evidence honestly.
- **Completion evidence:** case → test/fixture → observed red (or documented existing-behavior exception) → green, with commands and log paths in the result. Passing tests alone do not prove this contract was followed.

### Defined tests (write before production changes)
1. For identity/front, top and a known quarter-turn rotation, assert all six projected axis positions and back-to-front ordering, including overlapping front/back balls.
2. For each ±axis action assert the correct camera preset; clicking the active axis flips to its opposite.
3. Injected orientation updates change projected positions; unchanged rotations do not republish; a gizmo drag changes camera orientation. Hosted accessibility actions cover all six views.

### TDD verification
Focused command: `./scripts/dev.sh test -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/NavigationGizmoTests` (reuse/extend an existing suite if appropriate; confirm tests are discovered and executed, not zero tests). After green run `./scripts/dev.sh test` including unchanged pixel references. Use hand-computed expectations/independent Khronos output for renderer math, not values copied from the implementation.

For UI assertions prefer deterministic in-process hosted components and background AX selection; visual checks must inspect the actual rendered result. These instructions supersede older generic launch/uitest directions in this description: background only, no focus steal, no `--snapshot`, no leftover Export sheets; XCUITest requires explicit approval for that run. No app launch is required for this backlog edit.

name: Swap ThumbnailProvider to the web renderer behind a flag
description:
## Why

A unit test proves `WebStillRenderer` works in the **test host** process, which is a normal app. The spike's actual question is whether it works inside `ThumbnailExtension` — a sandboxed, non-UI app extension with its own seatbelt profile. Only running it there answers that.

## Approach

Edit `ThumbnailExtension/ThumbnailProvider.swift` in the worktree. Keep the RealityKit path intact and selectable — if the web path fails, being able to flip back in one line is how you tell "sandbox blocked it" apart from "the spike code is wrong".

Extensions do not inherit the shell environment, so `ProcessInfo.environment` is not a usable switch. Use a shared `UserDefaults` suite the host app can also write:

```swift
let useWeb = UserDefaults(suiteName: "lol.mattias.gltf-inspector.spike")?
    .bool(forKey: "WebThumbnail") ?? false
```

Set it from the terminal before testing:

```bash
defaults write lol.mattias.gltf-inspector.spike WebThumbnail -bool YES
```

Keep the reply mechanism exactly as it is. `ThumbnailProvider.swift` already documents that `QLThumbnailReply(imageFileURL:)` is the path Finder reliably consumes and that the `CGContext` drawing reply fails with `QLThumbnailError 102` for the generator path Finder uses. Do not "improve" this — write the PNG to `temporaryDirectory` and hand back the URL, same as today. Reuse `sweepStaleThumbnails()` unchanged.

### Entitlements

`ThumbnailExtension/ThumbnailExtension.entitlements` currently grants `app-sandbox`, user-selected + downloads read-only, and a home-relative read-only temporary exception.

**Start by changing nothing.** Whether the stock entitlement set is enough is part of what the spike is measuring. If WebContent fails to spawn, *then* try additions one at a time and record which one was needed — that finding is a deliverable. `com.apple.security.network.client` is the usual first suspect even though nothing here touches the network, because `WKWebView` spawns a Networking XPC service.

## Acceptance criteria

- With the default `NO`, thumbnails behave exactly as on `main` — no regression.
- With `YES`, the extension takes the `WebStillRenderer` path; confirmed in `log stream` on the `webthumb` category, not inferred from the image.
- Both paths compile; `./scripts/dev.sh install` in the worktree succeeds.
- The flip between paths is one `defaults write`, no rebuild.
result:
## Done

`ThumbnailProvider.provideThumbnail` gains an early branch to `renderWithWebGL` when the flag is on. The RealityKit path below it is byte-for-byte unchanged.

```bash
defaults write lol.mattias.gltf-inspector.spike WebThumbnail -bool YES   # web
defaults write lol.mattias.gltf-inspector.spike WebThumbnail -bool NO    # RealityKit
```

Read via `UserDefaults(suiteName: "lol.mattias.gltf-inspector.spike")`, defaulting to `false` — extensions do not inherit the shell environment, so `ProcessInfo.environment` was not an option. No rebuild needed to flip.

Reply mechanism deliberately identical to the RealityKit path: write the PNG into `temporaryDirectory`, hand back `QLThumbnailReply(imageFileURL:)`. The existing comment in this file records that the `CGContext` drawing reply works under `qlmanage -x` but fails with `QLThumbnailError 102` on the generator path Finder uses — so this was left alone rather than "improved". `sweepStaleThumbnails()` still runs for both paths.

Logging on the `webthumb` category brackets the work: `web thumbnail start <file> <px>` then `web thumbnail ready <file> <total>ms (<page>ms in page)`, so the Finder run yields per-file timings and tells the two renderers apart from the log alone rather than by eyeballing images.

**Entitlements deliberately unchanged.** Whether the stock set is enough is part of what the next subtask measures.

## Verification

- `xcodebuild -scheme GLTFInspector build` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**, no warnings.
- `WebStillRenderer.swift` and `StillRenderer.swift` both land in `ThumbnailExtension` via the existing `Shared/*.swift` glob; neither is in that target's `excludes` list, so no `project.yml` change was needed.
- Both code paths compile; the flag is read at call time, not cached, so flipping it takes effect on the next thumbnail request.

Not yet verified: that the web path actually *runs* under the extension sandbox. That is the next subtask and the whole point of the spike.

Committed as `1a5e1e2` on `spike/web-thumbnail`.

## Why

The one component the spike actually tests: render a GLB to PNG bytes through `WKWebView` with **no window**, in a process that has no UI. Everything else is plumbing around it.

## Approach

New file in the worktree: `Shared/WebStillRenderer.swift`. Mirror the shape of the existing `Shared/StillRenderer.swift` so a later swap is mechanical — construct with a URL and a pixel size, `await` a `CGImage`.

```swift
@MainActor
final class WebStillRenderer {
    init(model: URL, pixelSize: Int)
    func capture() async throws -> CGImage
}
```

### Serving local bytes

Do **not** use `loadFileURL` + `fetch()`. `file://` requests are blocked by CORS in `WKWebView` and the workarounds are worse than the fix.

Register a `WKURLSchemeHandler` on a private scheme (`gltf-inspector:`) that serves:

- `/renderer/*` from `Vendor/web-renderer/` in the extension bundle
- `/model.glb` from the requested file URL, read **inside the security scope**

Send a real `HTTPURLResponse` with a correct `Content-Type` (`text/javascript` for `.js`, `text/html` for `.html`) and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. A wrong MIME type on the ESM files makes the import map fail silently with a blank page.

This is also the right production architecture, not a spike shortcut: bytes flow through Swift, so security-scoped access and sidecar resolution stay in Swift where they already work.

### Getting pixels back

Page posts `{ png: "data:image/png;base64,..." }` over `WKScriptMessageHandler`. Decode to `NSBitmapImageRep` → `CGImage`.

Prefer `canvas.toDataURL()` over `WKWebView.takeSnapshot`. Both were confirmed working offscreen, but `toDataURL` reads the WebGL drawing buffer directly and does not depend on the view being layer-backed or window-hosted — which is exactly the property under test.

### Handling failure honestly

The whole point is to learn *how* this fails under the sandbox. Wire up and log, do not swallow:

- `WKNavigationDelegate`: `didFailProvisionalNavigation`, `didFail`
- `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` — **the signal that the sandbox killed WebContent**, and the single most likely no-go outcome
- a hard timeout (10 s) that reports "no message received" distinctly from an error
- `webView.configuration.websiteDataStore = .nonPersistent()` so the extension writes no cache into the container

Log through `AppLog` with a `webthumb` category so `log stream` picks it up from the extension.

## Acceptance criteria

- A unit test in `GLTFInspectorTests` renders `TestModels/Khronos samples/BoomBox/BoomBox.glb` through `WebStillRenderer` and asserts the result is 512x512 with **more than 100 distinct sampled colours** (a blank or single-colour image is the failure this guards).
- Test passes under `xcodebuild ... -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/WebStillRendererTests test`.
- Every failure path above logs a distinguishable message; verified by pointing it at `TestModels/Fixture Models/corrupt/truncated.glb` and confirming it fails with a real error rather than hanging.

## Reference

A working prototype of exactly this exists at `bench.swift` / `thumb.swift` in the scratchpad of the originating session, including the scheme handler and the distinct-colour check. If unavailable, everything needed to rebuild it is in this description.
result:
## Done

`Shared/WebStillRenderer.swift` — same shape as `StillRenderer` (construct with a URL and pixel size, `await capture()`), so the thumbnail path can swap between them on one flag.

- `WKWebView` created with a frame but **never added to a window** — the property under test.
- Pixels via `canvas.toDataURL()`, not `takeSnapshot`, so the result does not depend on the view being layer-backed or on screen.
- `LocalResourceHandler` serves `/renderer/*` from the bundle and `/model` from the file over a private `gltf-inspector:` scheme. Path traversal rejected; resolved paths confined to the bundled renderer folder. Security-scoped access stays in Swift and the page never sees a filesystem path.
- `websiteDataStore = .nonPersistent()` so the extension writes no cache into its container.
- New `AppLog.webThumb` category (subsystem `lol.mattias.gltf-inspector`, category `webthumb`).

Failure paths all resolve to a distinct error instead of hanging: `timedOut`, `webContentTerminated` (expected shape of a seatbelt denial), `navigationFailed`, `pageError(stage:message:)`, `missingRendererBundle`, `undecodableImage`. `finish()` resolves the continuation exactly once — timeout, WebContent death and the page's own error handler can all fire for one cause.

## Verification

`xcodebuild -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/WebStillRendererTests test` → **3 tests, all passed**.

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `rendersBoomBoxOffscreen` | 512x512, 6036 triangles, 1 draw call, **399 ms in page** |
| `failsLoudlyOnCorruptFile` | throws `pageError(stage: "parse", "Length out of range of buffer")` in 0.1 s — real error, not a timeout |
| `rendererBundleKeepsNestedLayout` | all 6 resources present at their nested paths |

Proof image `/tmp/web-still-boombox.png`, inspected visually: fully lit PBR, correct materials, transparent background, correctly framed.

Two bugs found by looking at the image rather than trusting the assertions:

1. First render was an almost-black silhouette. Cause was the probe, not WebGL — `PMREMGenerator.fromScene` renders scene *geometry*, so a scene holding only a `HemisphereLight` yields a black environment. `RoomEnvironment` fixed it; now commented in `thumb.html`.
2. Framing was cropped. Replaced the guessed camera distance with `radius / sin(fov/2) * 1.08`, reusing the same `1.08` as `PreviewCamera.thumbnailFitPadding` so both paths frame alike.

> The distinct-colour assertion (`> 100`) passed in **both** cases, including the black silhouette. It catches a blank buffer, not a dark render. Do not treat it as the only gate downstream.

Committed as `adcab0c` on `spike/web-thumbnail`.

## Caveats carried forward

- This ran in the **test host**, a normal app, not a sandboxed extension. The RBS warnings in the log (`doesn't have entitlement com.apple.runningboard.assertions.webkit`) are benign here but are the class of thing that may bite inside the extension.
- `TestModels/Khronos samples/` is gitignored, so a fresh worktree has none. A **symlink is not enough** — `FileManager.enumerator` does not descend a symlinked root, so `TestModels.hasKhronosSamples` stayed false and the BoomBox test silently skipped while the suite still reported "passed". Replaced with a real 46 MB copy.
- **`.dex/` lives only in the repo root**, not in the worktree. Run dex commands from `/Users/mattias/dev/glb-preview`, e.g. `(cd /Users/mattias/dev/glb-preview && dex ...)`.

name: EXP-014: Direct bufferView→SIMD floats (skip packed NSData)
description:
## Rank
impact × confidence × simplicity: **high × med-high × high** (one file; corpus mesh attrs are tight-packed floats; ~tens of MB redundant pack copies on 06–08)

## Classification
**NEW** (not a re-do of EXP-006-v2 packed-SIMD / delete-grouped). Same file, different mechanism: remove `GLTFPackedDataForAccessor` intermediate.

## Hypothesis
I believe `Packed.float*Array` still pays a full tightly-packed `malloc`+`memcpy` via `GLTFPackedDataForAccessor` before expanding into `[SIMDn]`, and reading float accessors straight from `bufferView.buffer.data` (memcpy for float2/4; one-pass expand for float3) will cut convert time on high-vert assets beyond noise vs cp-001.

## Parent champion
cp-001 / tip `1329a23` / `sum_median_total_ms=7620.2`

## Focus lane
**B** — parse · accessors · decode (buffers / accessors). No Draco/Meshopt in corpus-v2 (0/10); residual is float accessor unpack.

## Research basis
- GLTFKit2 `GLTFPackedDataForAccessor` ([GLTFAsset.m](https://github.com/warrenm/GLTFKit2/blob/e69e354c4f31ea07b7816b8cbe2ddb28e897d073/GLTFKit2/GLTFKit2/GLTFAsset.m)): always allocates packed `NSData`; tight path is still malloc+memcpy ([docs/examples](https://context7.com/warrenm/gltfkit2/llms.txt)).
- Corpus mesh attribute accessors are **tight** (stride == element size) on 04–10; vegetation alone ~77 MB of packed attribute bytes recopied.
- Swift `SIMD3<Float>` is not 12-byte packed ([SO / Metal layouts](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74314930/how-to-deal-with-the-lack-of-simd-packed-float3-in-swift)) → float3 needs expand, but **without** the intermediate packed buffer; float2/4 can memcpy like existing `ushort4Array` / `float4x4` direct paths in `PackedAccessors.swift`.
- glTF accessors are typed views over bufferViews ([Khronos glTF 2.0](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html)).

## Approach (one change)
In `Packed.floatData` / `packedFloats` (or float2/3/4 helpers): for `componentType == .float`, non-sparse, with `bufferView`, read source bytes with stride (treat 0 / elementSize as tight) directly into the destination SIMD array; keep `GLTFPackedDataForAccessor` + `GLTFTransformPackedDataToFloat` only for integer/normalized/sparse fallbacks.

## Likely files
- `Shared/PackedAccessors.swift` only

## Done when
- Implemented on worktree from `1329a23`
- Full 10-asset `load-bench` vs recorded control; KEEP only if beyond noise + correct + simple
- No quality skips; morph/skin/animation accessors still match

## Forbidden
- Do **not** re-land EXP-006-v2 “packed SIMD / delete grouped” as the change
- No EXP-008 / EXP-010 / EXP-012 style texture/ARGB/swizzle/UV claims
- No Draco/Meshopt-only opts (corpus has none)
- No prepare-skip / animation-disable / outliner-skip
result: Decision REJECT. Candidate 7396.7 vs recorded_control 7620.2 (−223 ms / −2.93%). |delta| under 3% noise (~229 ms) and only 5/10 faster (not ≥8/10). 0/10 errors. Closest in batch but not staged. Worktree+branch discarded. Artifacts: experiments/results/EXP-014.json

name: EXP-021: Stream ushort indices into LowLevelMesh (skip [UInt32] pack)
description:
## Rank
impact × confidence × simplicity: high — clear residual on EXP-017 path; Apple documents LowLevelMesh.Descriptor.indexType (MTLIndexType.uint16|uint32); fewest files (mesh convert only).

## Classification
VARIANT (of EXP-017 LowLevelMesh packed path; orthogonal to float3/float4 attribute memcpy)

## Hypothesis
After EXP-017 packed float3/float4 vertex memcpy, index convert still pays Packed.uint32Array (ushort/ubyte→uint32 widen into an intermediate [UInt32]) then a second memcpy into LowLevelMesh indices with indexType: .uint32. Streaming widen (or indexType: .uint16 + direct bufferView memcpy when totalVertices ≤ 65535 and indices are UNSIGNED_SHORT) removes that allocation/copy on high-tri assets 06/07/08 beyond noise.

## Parent champion
cp-001 @ 7620.2 ms (BATCH_CHAMPION_SHA 1329a23); build atop staged EXP-017 LowLevelMesh path (accepted_queue sha 2efb16f0872843f8e58b6a3395b77c46cc91622e), not tip-only MeshBuffers.

## Focus lane
B (parse · accessors · decode)

## Research basis
- Apple: LowLevelMesh.Descriptor indexType → MTLIndexType (uint16/uint32) — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/lowlevelmesh/descriptor-swift.struct/indextype
- Apple: LowLevelMesh descriptor init with indexType — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/lowlevelmesh/descriptor-swift.struct/init(vertexcapacity:vertexattributes:vertexlayouts:indexcapacity:indextype:)
- Metal MTLIndexType — native 16-bit indices; glTF UNSIGNED_SHORT maps cleanly
- Khronos/glTF: UNSIGNED_SHORT is the common index component
- Code residual in staged EXP-017: Packed.uint32Array → indices: [UInt32] → withUnsafeMutableIndices memcpy (.worktrees/exp-017/.../RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift)

## Approach (one change)
In convertPackedFloat3Mesh only: stop materializing [UInt32] via Packed.uint32Array. Prefer indexType: .uint16 + memcpy from tight UNSIGNED_SHORT bufferView when safe (totalVertices ≤ 65535, non-sparse, no meshopt); else stream ushort/ubyte→uint32 widen directly into withUnsafeMutableIndices (apply vertexBase while writing). Keep UNSIGNED_INT as memcpy. Fall back if layout unsafe.

## Likely files
- Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift (EXP-017 packed path)
- Optionally Shared/PackedAccessors.swift only if a tiny shared stream helper is cleaner than inline

## Done when
- LABEL=EXP-021 load-bench vs same-machine cp-001 / EXP-017-aware control
- KEEP only if |Δ| ≥ ~3% (~229 ms at 7620) or ≥8/10 same direction; concentrated on 06/07/08 OK
- Correctness: existing mesh/scene tests + 0/10 bench errors; topology unchanged

## Forbidden
- Do not re-try EXP-014 direct float accessor→SIMD pack
- Do not duplicate EXP-017 float3/float4 attribute memcpy
- No quality cuts; no skip prepare/animations/document; no corpus special-case; no interleaved-deinterleave mega rewrite in this EXP
result: REJECT incremental vs EXP-017: +1169.8 ms (+16.6%) vs 7066.1; 0/10 faster; undoes 06/07/08 packed wins. Leave EXP-017 staged. Discard worktree.

3. Change camera and selection: edge positions follow the current ID buffer without stale outlines. Default references stay unchanged.

Focused command: `./scripts/dev.sh test -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/SelectionOutlineTests` (reuse/extend an existing suite if appropriate; confirm tests are discovered and executed, not zero tests). name: EXP-013: JSON-only prepare BIN passthrough
description:
## Rank
impact × confidence × simplicity — high for prepare-hit 09 (~2.0s of 7.6s sum); medium confidence (EXP-005-v2 showed write+reread alone ≈0 on clean 09, but full parse+serialize of untouched BIN was never removed); simple (few files, no fidelity change).

## Classification
NEW (cheaper prepare VARIANT allowed by EXP-004 reject; **not** EXP-005/005-v2 GLTFAsset(data:) retry)

## Hypothesis
On cp-001, only `09-realistic_animals` fires prepare (67× `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`). `MetalRoughPrepare.shouldBakeTextures` returns false when `images > 40` (09 has 61), so prepare is a **JSON-only** rewrite — BIN bytes are unchanged — yet `prepareGLB` still `Data(contentsOf:)` + `GLBBox.parse` + full `serialize` (~208MB) before `writePrepared`. I believe skipping BIN materialization (peek JSON → metalRough JSON transform → write new JSON chunk + **copy BIN chunk from the source file**) cuts prepare I/O/alloc on 09 without skipping required prepare.

## Parent champion
cp-001 / tip `1329a23` / sum_median_total_ms=7620.2

## Focus lane
A — I/O · prepare · EntityLoader

## Research basis
- In-repo: `EntityLoader.prepareGLB` always full-reads; `MetalRoughPrepare.shouldBakeTextures` (`images > 40` → no bake); corpus 09 role = specular-gloss prepare hit
- [glTF 2.0 GLB container](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html) — JSON and BIN chunks are independent; BIN may be copied verbatim when JSON-only transforms leave bufferViews untouched
- EXP-005-v2: `GLTFAsset(data:)` after full serialize was not prepare-concentrated / confirmatory 09 ≈+8ms — do **not** retry that claim; this EXP targets **avoiding BIN load+serialize**, not post-serialize URL vs data

## Approach (one change)
Add a JSON-only prepare fast path when `MetalRoughPrepare.needsConversion` && `!RealityPrepare.needsPrepare` && bake would be skipped: transform peeked JSON only; write prepared GLB by splicing new padded JSON chunk + streaming/copying the original BIN chunk (FileHandle/`copyfile`) without ever holding the full BIN in a `Data` for parse/serialize. Fall back to today’s full parse path when RealityPrepare or texture bake needs BIN.

## Likely files
- `Shared/EntityLoader.swift`
- `Shared/GLBBox.swift`
- possibly thin helper in `Shared/MetalRoughPrepare.swift` (bake-gate query without mutating)

## Done when
- Same-machine bench vs recorded control `1329a23`; KEEP only if beyond noise **and** delta concentrates on prepare-hit 09 (report 09 Δ vs sum Δ)
- Prepare still runs (spec/gloss → metal/rough); no prepare-skip; Loader/prepare tests green
- Not a rehash of EXP-005 `GLTFAsset(data:)`

## Forbidden
- EXP-004/005 prepare skip; EXP-005-v2 dirty prepare / GLTFAsset(data:) same claim
- EXP-008 / EXP-010 / EXP-012
- Quality cuts; corpus special-case; inventing Lane B/C work
result: Decision REJECT. Candidate 7663.3 vs recorded_control 7620.2 (+43 ms / +0.57%, inside 3% noise ~229 ms). 0/10 errors. Prepare-hit 09 +18.5 ms — not concentrated. Worktree+branch discarded. Artifacts: experiments/results/EXP-013.json

name: EXP-018: Concurrent async TextureResource prefetch
description:
## Rank
1 (lane C — best impact × confidence × simplicity after cp-001 texture REJECTS)

## Classification
NEW

## Hypothesis
I believe residual load on texture-heavy 09/10 is dominated by **serial** `TextureResource.generate(from: CGImage)` for unique raster images (61 / 57 images), and overlapping RealityKit’s **async** CGImage→TextureResource path (TaskGroup / concurrent async inits) will cut wall-clock `total_load_ms` without changing mip/fidelity or upload backend.

## Parent champion
cp-001 (`1329a23`, sum_median_total_ms=7620.2)

## Focus lane
C — textures · materials · scene · still

## Research basis (links)
- Champion concentration: 09+10 ≈ 4985 ms (65% of sum) — `/tmp/glb-preview-load-bench/20260820-050719-cp-001.json`; corpus roles many materials/textures (`experiments/corpus.json`).
- Local: `Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift` — raster path sync `TextureResource.generate(from:options:)`; already caches by `(image.identifier, ColorMask)` but fills **serially** during material convert.
- Apple: [TextureResource.init(named:in:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/textureresource/init(named:in:)) — “Load textures concurrently with other content for optimal load times”; same guidance applies to in-memory async create.
- Apple: [TextureResource.init(image:withName:options:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/textureresource/init(image:withname:options:)) / async `generate(from:named:options:)` — async CGImage → TextureResource.
- Swift: [TaskGroup](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/taskgroup) for dynamic concurrent loads.
- EXP-015 REJECT: alternate **Metal/LowLevel upload** for `.all` was slower — do **not** change upload backend; only schedule/overlap RealityKit generate.
- EXP-010/008 REJECT: scalar swizzle / ARGB sibling-cache — out of scope; residual after EXP-009/015 notes points at `.all` serial generates.

## Approach (one change)
Before (or as a first phase of) scene material convert, collect unique `(GLTFImage.identifier, ColorMask, semantic)` keys required by `asset.materials`, decode/cached-CGImage as today, then **concurrently** create `TextureResource`s via async `TextureResource(image:withName:options:)` (or async `generate`) into the existing `textureResourcesForImageIdentifiers` cache. Keep sync `texture(for:)` as cache hit / fallback. No mipmapsMode downgrade, no resolution change, no LowLevel/MTK upload rewrite.

## Likely files
- `Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift`
- `Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert.swift` (await prefetch once per convert)
- Possibly `Shared/EntityLoader.swift` if convert entry must become async
- Tests only if needed for cache key coverage

## Done when
- `LABEL=EXP-018` full corpus bench vs same-machine / recorded_control cp-001 @ `1329a23`
- KEEP only if beyond noise (~3% / ~229 ms) with concentration on 09/10; 0/10 errors; mips + channel mapping unchanged
- Ledgers updated; REJECT discards worktree

## Forbidden
- Retry EXP-008 ARGB sibling-cache, EXP-010 LowLevel swizzle, EXP-012 UV fuse, EXP-015 MTK/LowLevel full-RGBA upload
- `mipmapsMode: .none` / resolution cuts / skipping required maps
- Prepare-skip, corpus special-case, v1-as-v2
- Parallel load-bench; merge to champion (implementer/benchmarker only)
result: REJECT +562 ms (+7.4%) SM; 05 +568; 09/10 no win. Worktree discarded.

name: EXP-027: lossless none+none texture CreateOptions
description:
## Rank
high × medium × high (09/10 ≈ 70% of cp-002 residual; 1 file)

## Classification
NEW (interaction cell never benched — not a blind retry of 019 or 022 alone)

## Hypothesis
TextureResource.generate on 09/10’s 61 PNG / 57 JPEG rasters still dominates residual (~5139 ms of 7372). EXP-022 (compression:.none + default mip pyramid) regressed because an uncompressed full mip chain uploads ~4/3× base pixels; EXP-019 (mipmapsMode:.none + default compression) was only −104 ms under noise. Pairing lossless compression:.none with mipmapsMode:.none should skip both CPU block-compress and the uncompressed mip pyramid while keeping full base resolution (non-lossy).

## Parent champion
cp-002 @ 1aceeda, sum_median_total_ms=7372.906

## Focus lane
C

## Research basis
- cp-002: 10 = 3148.9 ms (42.7%), 09 = 1990.2 ms (27.0%)
- Apple TextureResource.CreateOptions: independent compression + mipmapsMode
- Uncompressed ≈ channels×w×h×4/3 with auto mips
- Ledger gap: never benched compression.none ∧ mipmapsMode.none

## Approach
In RealityKitResourceContext raster (+ opacity) CreateOptions, pass compression: .none, mipmapsMode: .none. KTX2 path unchanged.

## Likely files
Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift only

## Done when
full v2 bench vs cp-002; KEEP iff beyond ~3% noise (~221 ms) or ≥8/10; 09/10 must not regress like EXP-022; base-res retained

## Forbidden
ASTC/lossy; retry 019 or 022 alone; 018/010/015; quality cuts / resolution cuts; prepare-skip; corpus special-case
result: REJECT −67.8 ms (−0.92%) vs cp-002 7372.9; under ~221 ms noise; 6/10 faster; 09 +12 / 10 −51; no EXP-022-style collapse. Worktree+branch removed.

name: EXP-029: Cap skeletal densify at ≤30fps
description:
## Rank
impact × confidence × simplicity — high × medium-high × high

## Classification
VARIANT-of-002 (cheaper sampling; explicitly allowed)

## Hypothesis
Skeletal SampledAnimation densification currently merges joint sample intervals with `min(...)` and allows `minimumInterval = 1/120`. Dense glTF keys on 03/05/10 force ~87 / ~50 / ~54 fps densify (~757 / ~1400 / ~817 frames). Flooring densify at `defaultInterval` (1/30) — never finer than 30 fps — cuts JointTransforms frame counts ~1.7–2.9× on those clips without skipping clips or changing mesh/texture/prepare paths.

## Parent champion
cp-002 · 7372.9 ms @ 1aceeda

## Focus lane
FULL PIPELINE residual (animation densify on 03/05/10; 09/texture cells exhausted; EXP-028 joints mesh in flight — do not touch)

## Research basis
- Protocol: EXP-002 REJECT allows VARIANT=cheaper sampling
- Corpus peek: 03/05/10 unique anim channels 173/235/305; durations ~8.7s / 28s / 15.2s; merged intervals ≈0.011 / 0.020 / 0.019 s (~87 / 50 / 54 fps)
- Code: `AnimationSampling.minimumInterval` + `mergeSampleInterval` min-merge; `RealityKitConvert+Animation` skeletal SampledAnimation loop
- Apple: SampledAnimation requires constant `frameInterval` (dense grid unavoidable; rate is the lever)
- https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/sampledanimation

## Approach
One policy change: raise floor so densify never exceeds 30 fps (set `minimumInterval = defaultInterval` and/or clamp `mergeSampleInterval` / `sampleInterval` so averageKeyDuration cannot push below 1/30). Keep morph / non-joint paths under the same cap. No clip skipping; no prepare/texture/LowLevelMesh edits.

## Likely files
Shared/AnimationHelpers.swift (optional touch: Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Animation.swift literals only if needed for morph max)

## Done when
LABEL=EXP-029 vs cp-002 beyond noise (≥3% or 8/10 same direction); AnimationSamplingTests + SceneGraph/Morph convert tests pass; clips still present on 03/05/10

## Forbidden
skip animations / prepare; quality cuts (ASTC, downsample); EXP-028 JOINTS/WEIGHTS fuse; EXP-018 concurrent textures; EXP-019/022/027 CreateOptions redo; EXP-007 min/max inputRange redo
result: ACCEPTED-STAGED: KEEP −243.4 ms (−3.30%) vs cp-002 7372.9 → 7129.5. Beyond ~221 ms noise. Concentrated on skinned/anim 03 −51 / 05 −75 / 10 −123 (−249 of total); 08 −53. 4/10 faster. AnimationSamplingTests 8/8; 0/10 bench errors. Staged accepted_queue; worktree .worktrees/exp-029 retained @ e58473a. No merge.

name: EXP-030: no-copy ImageIO bufferView raster decode
description:
## Rank
residual_share(08=10.5%, texture spill 09/10) × evidence(GLTFKit2 CFDataCreate + residual phases + 08 anatomy) × simplicity(one Shared context path) — prefer over Metal-upload/CreateOptions folklore.

## Classification
NEW

## Hypothesis
GLTFKit2 `GLTFImage.newCGImage` always `CFDataCreate`-copies each bufferView image (08 alone ~80MB PNG; 09+10 ~434MB embedded) then `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex(..., NULL)`, so decode may stay deferred into `TextureResource.generate`. Replacing that path with a no-copy byte view + `kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately` should cut **(08-cinema_projector, texture|decode)** (~630ms texture nested in 772 decode) and concentrate on 09/10 texture without alternate upload APIs.

## Parent champion
cp-003 / `173fc71f3e366dc26b8323d98ccecc228a16c8b5` / 7464.8 ms (noise ~224 ms)

## Focus lane
B (parse·decode) — residual texture nested under decode

## Residual cell
**(08-cinema_projector, texture|decode)** — must name 08; secondary concentration 09/10 texture if ImageIO copy/decode tax scales with embedded rasters.

## Research basis
- `experiments/residual-map.json` cp-003: 08 share 10.5%, texture_ms 629.7 / decode_ms 772.4 / scene 776; corpus parse sum only 138ms
- Asset anatomy: single 8192×8192 RGB PNG (~80.1MB bufferView), 1 material (emissive shares albedo — already ignored), 14 meshes
- warrenm/GLTFKit2 `GLTFAsset.m` `newCGImage`: `CFDataCreate` of full bufferView then ImageIO with NULL options; does not populate `cachedImage` on that path
- Apple/ImageIO practice: `ShouldCacheImmediately` to force one bitmap decode (widely used in production Swift)
- Not retrying EXP-015/018/019/022/027 (Metal blit / concurrent prefetch / CreateOptions*)

## Approach (one change)
In `RealityKitResourceContext`, for bufferView-backed non-KTX2 rasters, build `CGImage` via ImageIO from a no-copy view of `buffer.data[offset..<offset+length]` with `kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately: true` (source `ShouldCache: false`); cache as today; keep existing `TextureResource.generate` + scalar vImage path; fall back to `newCGImage()` on failure.

## Likely files
- `Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift`

## Done when
`LABEL=EXP-030 ./scripts/load-bench.sh` vs cp-003 control; KEEP iff beyond ~3% noise (~224ms) with honest concentration on 08 (and/or 09/10 texture); else REJECT. No quality change (full-res, default CreateOptions).

## Forbidden
CreateOptions* (019/022/027); MTK/LowLevel alternate upload (015); concurrent texture prefetch (018); downsample/thumbnail quality cuts; fused UV (012/024); EXP-017/021/028/029 mesh/skin/densify paths; corpus special-case on 08 alone.
result: REJECT EXP-030: +339.5 ms (+4.55%) vs cp-003 control 7464.8 (noise ~224). 4/10 faster; inverted residual — 07 +90 / 08 +116 / 09 +146 / 10 −27. Correctness OK (0/10 errors). Worktree+branch discarded. accepted_queue unchanged; reject_only_batches=1. Must-not-retry: no-copy ImageIO bufferView decode w/o 08/09/10 win.

- The cases below are defined test contracts, not implemented tests or observed failures. Baseline: **not run for this backlog edit**. Use existing suites where they cover the behavior; proposed suite names are destinations, not existing files.
- **Red first:** after prerequisites are available, add the smallest deterministic behavioral test before its production change. name: Renderer: on-demand GPU pick pass returning the node under a pixel
description:
**Why:** the canvas needs to know which glTF node is under the cursor, exactly as drawn (skinning is baked into vertex buffers, alpha-mask cutouts must click through).

**Scope:**
- New fragment `khronos_pick_fragment` appended to `Renderer/Shaders/pbr.metal` (after the overlay shaders). Vertex stage: reuse `khronos_vertex` unchanged so positions match the main pass exactly. Fragment: compute base alpha like `khronos_fragment` (baseColor × vertex color × base color texture alpha via `materialTextures.maps[0]` when `m.flags.x & 1`), `discard_fragment()` when `m.flags.y == 1` (MASK) and alpha < `m.surface.w`; return `uint` draw index + 1 from a `constant uint &drawID [[buffer(6)]]`.
- `MetalRenderer.pick(_ options: ViewOptions, pose: MetalCameraPose, width:height:, centerOffset:, point: SIMD2<Int>) throws -> Int?` (glTF node index or nil). Render target `.r32Uint` + `.depth32Float` at the full canvas size (clear 0), same `GPUFrame` / viewport / file-camera / `centerOffset` setup as `renderTexture`: extract that setup into a shared private helper rather than copying it. Draw `order.main` after the Phase 1 draw filter (hidden draws are not pickable). Bind material uniforms + `MetalMaterialResources` like `encodeScene`. Read back one pixel (blit to a 1×1 shared buffer), map draw index → `scene.draws[i].nodeIndex`.
- Pipeline cached like `pipeline(blend:)`; pick runs only on demand, never per frame.

**Out:** gizmo picking (Phase 4), instance ids.
**Done when:** a pixel over a mesh returns its node; background → nil; alpha-mask hole → the mesh behind; through a file camera it returns what that camera shows; hidden nodes are skipped.
**Verification:** new `GLTFInspectorTests/MetalPickTests.swift`: in-memory GLB (see `TestGLBFixtures`) with two quads at different depths/positions, assert the centre pixels; a MASK quad with a transparent texture region over another; hiding the front quad returns the back one. `./scripts/dev.sh test` — all pixel references unchanged.

**Spec:** `.agents/plans/2026-11-04-scene-interaction.md` (coverage table + decisions log). Read `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md` first.
**Rules:** work on `main` unless told otherwise; never regenerate pixel references for a default render (`TestModels/References/`); new UI goes through `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/` components; check UI on screen yourself (`./scripts/dev.sh run <fixture>`, `screencapture`), never ask the user to test.
result: GPU pick pass: khronos_pick_fragment in pbr.metal; MetalRenderer.pick + sceneFrameSetup shared with renderTexture; encodePick writes drawIndex+1 to R32Uint. MetalPickTests: stacked quads, background nil, MASK hole through, file camera. ./scripts/dev.sh test → ** TEST SUCCEEDED ** (136 tests); pixel refs unchanged. Left: wire click→selection (qtuda1nk).

name: EXP-017: LowLevelMesh packed float3 attrs (skip SIMD3 pad)
description:
## Rank
impact×confidence×simplicity: high × medium × medium — corpus-v2 has millions of tightly packed float VEC3 (byteStride 12) on 06/07/08; MeshBuffers.Positions forces 12→16 SIMD3 expand after GLTFPacked. Distinct from REJECT’d EXP-014 (still built [SIMD3<Float>]).

## Classification
NEW

## Hypothesis
I believe MeshBuffers.Positions/Normals via Packed.float3Array’s 12-byte→padded SIMD3 expansion dominates residual convert on high-vert assets; RealityKit LowLevelMesh with MTLVertexFormat.float3 / packed_float3 layouts can memcpy glTF bufferViews as-is and cut sum_median_total_ms beyond noise without skipping required skin/morph/animation work.

## Parent champion
cp-001 (sum_median_total_ms=7620.179249000001, tip 1329a23)

## Focus lane
B (parse · accessors · decode / mesh attribute packing)

## Research basis
- WWDC24 “Build a spatial drawing app with RealityKit” — LowLevelMesh exists to bring GPU/custom vertex layouts to RealityKit as-is and avoid unnecessary conversions/copying: https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2024/10104/
- Apple LowLevelMesh: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/lowlevelmesh
- metal-by-example LowLevelMesh sample using packed_float3 position/normal + float2 UVs: https://github.com/metal-by-example/metal-spatial-dynamic-mesh
- Corpus probe: 06/07/08 float VEC3 almost entirely byteStride=12 (tight pack); no KHR_draco in v2 (Draco decode EXPs would not move this bench)

## Approach (one change)
For non-skinned, non-morph triangle primitives whose POSITION/NORMAL/(optional TANGENT)/TEXCOORD_0 are non-sparse float accessors with tight strides, build a LowLevelMesh (separate or interleaved layouts with MTLVertexFormat.float3 / float2), memcpy from bufferView bytes, wrap as MeshResource; fall back to existing MeshResource.Part + Packed.* path for skins, morph targets, points, sparse, normalized/int, or failed LowLevel create.

## Likely files
- Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift (primary)
- Possibly tiny helper in Shared/PackedAccessors.swift only if needed for stride/offset validation (prefer keep logic in Mesh convert)

## Done when
- Candidate LABEL=EXP-017 load-bench vs recorded_control cp-001 on corpus-v2
- Decision KEEP only if |delta| ≥ 3% of control (~229ms) OR same direction on ≥8/10; else REJECT
- Skinned (03/05/10) and morph (10) still load; AnimationSampling/SceneGraph/Mesh tests green
- No prepare-skip, no includeAnimations=false, no corpus special-case

## Forbidden
- Retry EXP-014 direct bufferView→[SIMD3<Float>] pack skip without new ≥8/10 or beyond-noise evidence
- Quality cuts; disable clips/skins/morph; prepare-skip; v1-as-v2; invent EXPs for lanes A/C
result: ACCEPTED-STAGED −554 ms (−7.3%) SM; 9/10; 06/07/08 concentrated. Staged to accepted_queue; worktree kept for checkpoint.

description:
# Plan: PreviewUI Component Library (Pattern B)

## Summary

Add `PreviewUI/Components/` for shared reusable UI, `PreviewSupport/` for mocks/fixtures, and `#Preview` on every view. Keep feature folders (`Inspector/`, `Sidebar/`, `Toolbar/`, `Overlays/`, `Frame/`, `Settings/`) for panels and shell. Single-window macOS app — no Screens/ folder, no atoms/molecules taxonomy.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- PreviewUI framework only — no `Shared/` import
- System fonts; `Theme.swift` for colors + layout metrics only (no type scale)
- `HostShellRootView` → `ShellRootView` API unchanged
- Previews are dev-time; `#Preview` + `PreviewSupport/` mocks, no catalog app, no SPM split
- Do not delete feature folders

## Ownership map

- **PreviewSupport/**: mocks + fixtures — no production UI
- **Components/**: shared reusables extracted from 2+ call sites or clear primitives
- **Feature folders**: domain-bound panels/sections/pills — compose Components

4. Sidebar / Inspector / Toolbar+Overlays previews (parallel after step 3)

6. Integration verify (`dev.sh test`, `dev.sh run cube`, preview audit)

- Final acceptance: `./scripts/dev.sh test`, `./scripts/dev.sh run cube`, `rg '#Preview' PreviewUI` (~120+)

## Success criteria

name: Skeleton overlay for a selected skin or joint
description:
**Why:** rigged files show nothing about their bones.

**Scope:** when the selection is a skin row (`NodeKind.skin`, index into `asset.skins`) or a node that is a joint of any skin, `overlayVertices` draws lines from each joint's world position to its parent joint's position (parent = nearest ancestor that is also a joint of the same skin), plus a small 3-axis cross per joint; selected joint gets the accent colour, others a light grey. Add `selectedSkin: Int?` to `MetalOverlayOptions`/`ViewOptions` from `ViewState.selection`. Layer list: joint nodes get a "joint" badge or glyph — add a `DSTypeIcon` role variant through the design system (`NodeKind` is display-only; derive "is joint" from `GLTFDocument.skins[].jointNames`/indices — add `jointNodeIndices: [Int]` to `GLTFDocument.Skin` in `GLTFCore/GLTFDocumentJSON.swift`).
**Out:** posed skeleton during animation (comes for free once Phase 6 updates world matrices — note it in the result).

**Done when:** selecting the skin in `rigged/two-joint-skin.gltf` shows two joints connected; selecting a joint highlights it.
**Verification:** unit test for joint segment count/positions on the rigged fixture; on-screen screenshot; `./scripts/dev.sh test`.

**Spec:** `.agents/plans/2026-11-04-scene-interaction.md` (coverage table + decisions log). Read `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md` first.
**Rules:** work on `main` unless told otherwise; never regenerate pixel references for a default render (`TestModels/References/`); new UI goes through `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/` components; check UI on screen yourself (`./scripts/dev.sh run <fixture>`, `screencapture`), never ask the user to test.

## TDD execution contract
- The cases below are defined test contracts, not implemented tests or observed failures. Baseline: **not run for this backlog edit**. Use existing suites where they cover the behavior; proposed suite names are destinations, not existing files.
- **Red first:** after prerequisites are available, add the smallest deterministic behavioral test before its production change. Run the focused suite and record test name, command, revision/worktree state, actual failing assertion and log path. A missing API/compiler error may guide initial scaffolding, but establish a compiling behavioral failure before implementation; build/tool/fixture errors are not feature-red evidence. Never use unconditional failures, skip/expected-failure markers, or loosen an oracle to manufacture red.
- **Green, then refactor:** implement only enough to pass that test, run the remaining cases, then refactor with tests green. Blocked leaves define tests now and establish executable red after their prerequisite lands; do not invent placeholder dependencies.
- For already implemented behavior, keep the regression green and, where safe, prove sensitivity using a temporary isolated mutation/reversion of only that behavior. Do not undo another worker's edits or claim retroactive red. Record unavailable red evidence honestly.
- **Completion evidence:** case → test/fixture → observed red (or documented existing-behavior exception) → green, with commands and log paths in the result. Passing tests alone do not prove this contract was followed.

### Defined tests (write before production changes)
1. Load rigged/two-joint-skin.gltf: assert two joint crosses and one bone segment at hand-computed world positions.
2. Insert a nonjoint ancestor between joints: connection targets the nearest ancestor joint in the same skin; a second skin does not create cross-skin bones.
3. Selecting a joint changes its highlight; selecting no skin/joint emits no skeleton overlay. A hidden subtree follows existing visibility rules.

### TDD verification
Focused command: `./scripts/dev.sh test -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/SkeletonOverlayTests` (reuse/extend an existing suite if appropriate; confirm tests are discovered and executed, not zero tests). After green run `./scripts/dev.sh test` including unchanged pixel references. Use hand-computed expectations/independent Khronos output for renderer math, not values copied from the implementation.

For UI assertions prefer deterministic in-process hosted components and background AX selection; visual checks must inspect the actual rendered result. These instructions supersede older generic launch/uitest directions in this description: background only, no focus steal, no `--snapshot`, no leftover Export sheets; XCUITest requires explicit approval for that run. No app launch is required for this backlog edit.

name: EXP-020: Mapped NSData → GLTFAsset(data:) on no-prepare path
description:
## Rank
Impact × confidence × simplicity: **High × Med-High × High** (fewest files). Best NEW lane-A candidate after prepare-lane ceiling (EXP-016 −187 ms under noise).

## Classification
NEW (not VARIANT of EXP-005/013/016)

## Hypothesis
I believe `GLTFAsset(url:)` heap-copies every no-prepare GLB because GLTFKit2 uses `NSData dataWithContentsOfURL:options:0`, and feeding a single `NSDataReadingMappedIfSafe`/`MappedAlways` blob into `GLTFAsset(data:)` removes that full-file memcpy on texture-heavy 07/08/10 (100–254 MB) without skipping prepare or touching textures.

## Parent champion
cp-001 @ `1329a23` — `sum_median_total_ms=7620.179249000001`

## Focus lane
A — I/O · prepare · EntityLoader

## Research basis
- GLTFKit2 `GLTFAssetReader.m` `syncLoadAssetWithURL:data:`: `internalData = data ?: [NSData dataWithContentsOfURL:assetURL options:(NSDataReadingOptions)0 …]` (unmapped full-file read on URL path).
- Apple `NSData.ReadingOptions.mappedIfSafe` / `mappedAlways` — map instead of copy when safe; prefer `NSData` over Swift `Data` if bridging drops mapping.
- EXP-005 / EXP-005-v2 only kept `GLTFAsset(data:)` on the **prepare-temp** path and left **URL for no-prepare**; must-not-retry is the prepare claim — this targets the complementary path.
- EXP-016 proved bake-gated metalRough prepare rewrite ceiling ≈ −187 ms under noise; residual dominated by large no-prepare + texture assets.
- Corpus: 10/07/08 no prepare; 09 still prepare-hit (leave prepared path alone).

## Approach (one change)
In `EntityLoader`: when `loadURL == originalURL` (no prepare rewrite), read once via `NSData(contentsOf:options:.mappedIfSafe)` and `GLTFAsset(data:options:)`. Keep `peekJSON` prepare gate. Do **not** change prepare serialize/write, metalRough, or texture upload.

## Likely files
- `Shared/EntityLoader.swift` (primary)
- optionally `Shared/GLBBox.swift` if peek-from-Data helps

## Done when
- `LABEL=EXP-020 ./scripts/load-bench.sh` vs same-machine cp-001
- KEEP if beyond noise (≥3% or ≥8/10); else REJECT
- Record in `experiments/results.json` + WHAT-WE-TRIED

## Forbidden
- Skip prepare / required convert work
- Retry EXP-005 prepare-temp Data claim without prepare-only metric
- Retry EXP-013 / EXP-016
- Quality cuts; corpus special-case; lane-C texture/mip changes; EXP-018 prefetch
result: REJECT +533 ms (+7.0%) vs tip control 7620.2; 0/10 faster; 09/10 regress. Control reused. Worktree discarded. accepted_queue still [EXP-017].

name: EXP-011: Cache materials by ObjectIdentifier
description:
## Rank
2

## Classification
VARIANT (of deleted pre-009 orchestrator-invented “material-once” queue — recreated only with citations)

## Hypothesis
I believe `convert(material:)` runs once per mesh primitive with no identity cache, so assets that reuse few materials across many meshes (07-vegetation: 93 meshes / 13 materials; also any shared-material multi-mesh assets) rebuild PBR/Unlit materials and re-enter `applyBlendMode`/`alphaUsage` repeatedly even though `TextureResource`s are already cached. Caching the converted RealityKit material by `ObjectIdentifier` (or `===`) of `GLTFMaterial` should cut residual convert cost after EXP-009’s opacity removal.

## Parent champion
EXP-009

## Research basis (links)
- Local hot path: `Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift` calls `self.convert(material: primitive.material, context:)` inside the per-primitive `compactMap` with **no** material cache (grep shows no `ObjectIdentifier` / material map in Shared/).
- Upstream same pattern: [warrenm/GLTFKit2 `GLTFRealityKit.swift`](https://github.com/warrenm/GLTFKit2/blob/master/GLTFKit2/GLTFKit2/GLTFRealityKit.swift) — identical per-primitive `convert(material:)` (no reuse).
- Khronos glTF tutorial — primitives reference materials by index / reuse: https://github.khronos.org/glTF-Tutorials/gltfTutorial/gltfTutorial_009_Meshes.html
- glTF Transform Material docs: “Materials should be reused wherever possible”: https://gltf-transform.dev/modules/core/classes/Material
- Corpus v2: `07-vegetation_pack` mesh_count=93, material_count=13 (`experiments/corpus.json`); profiler note in `WHAT-WE-TRIED.md` flagged residual material-once after opacity tax removal.

## Approach (one change)
Add a convert-session cache (on `RealityKitConvert` or `RealityKitResourceContext`) from `ObjectIdentifier(gltfMaterial)` → `any Material`. On cache hit, reuse the prior RealityKit material instance for that glTF material identity. Nil materials still use `defaultMaterial`. One behavioral change only — no mesh/texture/animation edits.

## Likely files
- `Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift`
- `Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Material.swift` and/or `Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert.swift` (cache storage)

## Done when
- Bench vs same-machine champion control; expect concentration on multi-mesh shared-material assets (esp. 07), not false wins on 1:1 mesh/material files alone.
- Correctness: shared materials still render; BLEND/MASK/cutout (EXP-009) behavior unchanged across reuse.
- KEEP/REJECT per PROTOCOL noise + complexity gates.

## Forbidden / out of scope
- Blind recreation without this evidence packet (already satisfied)
- Skipping materials, special-casing corpus IDs
- Combining with UV or texture EXPs in the same change
- Parallel benches; champion merge
result:
## Decision
KEEP

## Hypothesis
Cache converted RealityKit materials by ObjectIdentifier of GLTFMaterial so multi-mesh shared-material assets (esp. 07-vegetation 93 meshes / 13 materials) avoid rebuilding PBR materials repeatedly.

## Change
`RealityKitResourceContext` + `RealityKitConvert+Material.swift`: convert-session map ObjectIdentifier → any Material; nil materials still use defaultMaterial. applyBlendMode / EXP-009 cutout unchanged.

## Champion control
sum_median_total_ms = 8370.5 (LABEL=EXP-011-champ on main / EXP-009 tree)

## Candidate
sum_median_total_ms = 8001.7 (LABEL=EXP-011 @ 59c777a)

## Delta
−368.8 ms (−4.41%) vs same-machine control. Beyond 3% noise (~251 ms of control / ~232 ms of frozen 7732).

## Per-asset
07-vegetation −183.1 ms (−19.1%); 10-mecha −132.3 ms; 08 −33 / 09 −31 / 05 −16 / 06 −8; tiny flat; 02/03/04 small regressions (+2/+8/+24). 6/10 faster. Concentration on multi-mesh shared-material assets as hypothesized. Artifacts: experiments/results/EXP-011.json + EXP-011-champ.json

## Correctness
0/10 bench errors. TextureAlphaUsageTests pass. BLEND/MASK/cutout convert logic unchanged (cache hit returns same built material).

## Complexity
low (+17/−2) — justified by −4.4% / −369 ms.

## Reason
Beyond-noise win with expected 07 concentration; low complexity; no fidelity change.

## Must not retry
Blind material cache without ObjectIdentifier / shared-material evidence

## Worktree / SHA
KEEP — leave /Users/mattias/dev/glb-preview/.worktrees/exp-011 branch exp/EXP-011 commit 59c777a for orchestrator promote. Champion pointer NOT updated.

name: Bug/perf: RealityKit tight LowLevelMesh layout fails for 5+ attributes, falls back to slow MeshDescriptor
description:
## Why
W1 realitykit lane: TightLowLevelLayout.make (RendererRealityKit/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift ~535) puts each attribute in its own vertex buffer (up to 6); LowLevelMesh rejects vertexBufferCount 5, so position+normal+tangent+uv0+(uv1|color) meshes — common in real assets — hit the slower MeshDescriptor path and log 'tight float mesh convert failed: … invalid(vertexBufferCount: 5)'.
## Done when
Those meshes take the fast path (interleave or pack attributes into ≤ the allowed buffer count); no such log during dev.sh test; goldens unchanged.
## Verification
Failing test first (a 5-attribute primitive converts via LowLevelMesh); dev.sh test; goldens byte-identical; before/after convert time on a big sample (bench xlrxlm4o if landed).
result: Non-position attrs share LowLevelMesh buffer 1, so 5- and 6-attribute primitives stay on the fast path instead of invalid(vertexBufferCount: 5). Proof: fiveAttributePrimitiveConvertsViaLowLevelMesh, sixAttributePrimitiveConvertsViaLowLevelMesh. Merged to next-main (3d8481d). ./scripts/dev.sh test: 342 tests / 84 suites passed. Goldens unchanged; bench not run.

commit.message: Pack LowLevelMesh extras so 5+ attribute meshes stay on the fast path.

name: Spike: WebGL thumbnail from a sandboxed Quick Look extension
description:
## Why

Product goal: a pre-flight inspector for people working with glTF/GLB **for the web**. They need to see what the file actually contains and how it actually renders, *before* opening it in Blender or wiring it into a project. That makes renderer fidelity the product, not an implementation detail.

The current RealityKit convert path cannot deliver that. Measured against the working tree:

- `KHR_materials_transmission` is collapsed to opacity; `volume`, `iridescence`, `anisotropy`, `dispersion`, `diffuse_transmission` are logged as not rendered (`ConvertProblemReport.ignoredExtensions`).
- `sheen` is colour-only, `specular` is factor-only.
- `MetalRoughPrepare` + `RealityPrepare` (~802 lines) **rewrite the file before it renders**: re-bake spec-gloss textures, dequantize meshes, transcode WebP to PNG, expand GPU instancing.

For an inspector whose job is "does this file have a problem", showing the user artifacts our own conversion introduced is a correctness bug in the product.

A benchmark run (24 Aug 2026, Apple Silicon, macOS 26) also removed the usual objections:

| | RealityKit | WebKit + three.js |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BoomBox 10 MB, bytes to pixels | 163 ms | 236 ms |
| Corset 13 MB, parse only | 172–220 ms | 127–133 ms |
| One-time stack warm-up | ~510 ms | ~324 ms |
| Process family RSS | not measured | ~430 MB |

So speed is roughly a wash. The blocking constraint is a **product** one, stated by the user:

> We can't have one renderer for the thumbnail, one for Quick Look and another for the app. It all needs to look the same.

Finder thumbnail, Quick Look preview and the document window must be one renderer. Quick Look preview and the document window can both host a `WKWebView` — that is well-trodden. The Finder thumbnail is the risk: `QLThumbnailProvider` is non-UI and runs under a tighter sandbox.

## What was already proven (and what wasn't)

A throwaway CLI harness with `NSApplication.activationPolicy = .prohibited` and a `WKWebView` that is **never added to a window** rendered BoomBox correctly at 512x512 and returned real PNG bytes in 484–980 ms from cold process start. Both `canvas.toDataURL()` (with `preserveDrawingBuffer: true`) and `WKWebView.takeSnapshot` worked.

That disproves the folklore that offscreen `WKWebView` can't do WebGL — but **a CLI process is not a sandboxed app extension**. The extension seatbelt profile may block the WebContent or GPU XPC spawn. That single unknown decides the whole architecture.

## Done criteria

A correct, fully-lit PNG of a GLB, produced by a **real signed and installed `QLThumbnailProvider`** rendering through `WKWebView`, appearing **in Finder** (not `qlmanage`), within the thumbnail time budget — plus a written go/no-go with timings and observed failure modes.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Switching Quick Look preview or the document window. Thumbnail only.
- Choosing the production web renderer. The spike uses prebuilt three.js ESM because it needs no build step; the production recommendation is the Khronos glTF Sample Renderer (Apache-2.0, keeps `pbrSpecularGlossiness`, `KHR_materials_variants`, `KHR_animation_pointer`, and ships its own debug channels). That choice is a separate decision and must not be settled here.
- Matching the existing RealityKit look. The spike proves the mechanism, not the art direction.
- Deleting any RealityKit code. The existing path stays the default and stays working.

## Constraints

- Do not disturb the uncommitted work in the working tree. Spike on its own branch or worktree.
- `main` must keep shipping the RealityKit thumbnail. Nothing here merges to `main` without a separate decision.
- `qlmanage` hangs headless on this machine — Finder-driven verification only.
result:
## Verdict: GO

A WebGL renderer works inside the real signed, sandboxed `QLThumbnailProvider`, and Finder displays the results. The one-renderer constraint — thumbnail, Quick Look and document window must agree — is satisfiable by WebKit.

## The finding

Stock entitlements fail. Every request died with:

```
Sandbox: ThumbnailExtension(37619) deny(1) mach-issue-extension
  target:com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd
  extension-class:com.apple.webkit.extension.mach
```

WebContent could not start; `QLThumbnailError 102` on all four models.

**`com.apple.security.network.client` alone fixes it.** Isolated by adding it alongside `mach-lookup` exceptions, then removing those and re-testing. `WKWebView` spawns a Networking XPC service even though this page loads solely from a custom scheme handler and touches no network.

## Evidence

- Driven through `QLThumbnailGenerator.generateBestRepresentation`, the generator path Finder uses — `qlmanage` was avoided deliberately (it hangs headless here, and `-x` exercises a different reply path).
- Confirmed visually in Finder icon view: all four models correct — `/tmp/finder-icons.png`.
- WebGL output distinguishable from RealityKit at a glance: transparent background and lit emissive PLAY button vs opaque grey 0.94 and an unlit one. That difference caught two false positives.

| File | Web, via extension | RealityKit, same PNG size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BoomBox 10 MB | 1807 ms (773 in page) | 163–198 ms |
| BarramundiFish 12 MB | 1833 ms (1070 in page) | 154–197 ms |
| Corset 13 MB | 1841 ms (1081 in page) | 142–235 ms |
| tiny.glb | 292 ms (124 in page) | 19–20 ms |

WebKit is **4–8x slower on cold work**. Thumbnails are async and cached so this is not disqualifying, but it is the honest cost and it is recorded in the decision doc rather than buried.

## Output

`docs/decision-web-renderer.md` on `spike/web-thumbnail` (4 commits ahead of `3d2b374`). Follow-ups `3ejklvvg` (migration) and `w5m5lvzg` (production renderer choice) created. Nothing merged; `main` still ships RealityKit.

## Traps that cost real time

Two configurations reported success while RealityKit was silently rendering — caught only by looking at the image, not by any assertion:

1. `UserDefaults(suiteName:)` is invisible to a sandboxed extension (reads its own container).
2. `homeDirectoryForCurrentUser` and `NSHomeDirectory()` return the container home under the sandbox; `getpwuid(getuid())->pw_dir` gives the real one.

Also: the "distinct colours > 100" assertion passes on a near-black render; `PMREMGenerator.fromScene` renders geometry, so a light-only scene yields a black probe; and a sample-gated test that skips still reports the suite as passing.

## Machine state

`lsregister -dump` found **22 registered copies** of `glTF Inspector.app`, with `pluginkit` resolving the active thumbnail extension to a stale 22 Aug Xcode DerivedData build rather than `/Applications`. Any earlier thumbnail verification on this machine was testing an arbitrary old build. The 20 stale registrations were removed and `/Applications/glTF Inspector.app` is now the active provider — cleaner than before the spike. Marker file removed, Quick Look cache reset, temp folders deleted.

The repo root working tree is byte-identical to its pre-spike state: 12 modified files, 522 insertions / 496 deletions, plus untracked `Shared/PreviewSession.swift`. One commit briefly landed on `main` by mistake and was reverted with `git reset --mixed`; details in `mnlkj106`.
