name: Orbit around selection and zoom toward cursor
description:
**Why:** inspecting parts needs the pivot on the part and zoom where you point.
**Scope:** `Renderer/ModelView.swift` + `MetalUserCamera.swift`: when a node is selected, orbit target = its bounds centre (smooth retarget, no jump: keep eye, move target); scroll/pinch zoom dollies toward the pick-pass hit (or the ray point at the target depth) instead of the target. Settings toggles in `ViewSettingsPane` (default on).
**Done when:** select a corner part, orbit pivots around it; scrolling over a spot zooms into that spot.
**Verify:** unit tests on camera math; on screen.

**Context:** spec `.agents/plans/2026-11-04-scene-interaction.md`; read `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md`. New UI via `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/`. Verify: `./scripts/dev.sh test` green, references unchanged, check on screen yourself.

## TDD execution contract
- The cases below are defined test contracts, not implemented tests or observed failures. Baseline: **not run for this backlog edit**. Use existing suites where they cover the behavior; proposed suite names are destinations, not existing files.
- **Red first:** after prerequisites are available, add the smallest deterministic behavioral test before its production change. Run the focused suite and record test name, command, revision/worktree state, actual failing assertion and log path. A missing API/compiler error may guide initial scaffolding, but establish a compiling behavioral failure before implementation; build/tool/fixture errors are not feature-red evidence. Never use unconditional failures, skip/expected-failure markers, or loosen an oracle to manufacture red.
- **Green, then refactor:** implement only enough to pass that test, run the remaining cases, then refactor with tests green. Blocked leaves define tests now and establish executable red after their prerequisite lands; do not invent placeholder dependencies.
- For already implemented behavior, keep the regression green and, where safe, prove sensitivity using a temporary isolated mutation/reversion of only that behavior. Do not undo another worker's edits or claim retroactive red. Record unavailable red evidence honestly.
- **Completion evidence:** case → test/fixture → observed red (or documented existing-behavior exception) → green, with commands and log paths in the result. Passing tests alone do not prove this contract was followed.

### Defined tests (write before production changes)
1. Given a selected off-center subtree, retarget orbit to its bounds center while preserving eye position at the retarget boundary; subsequent orbit rotates around that center.
2. For an off-center cursor ray, dolly moves toward the hit (or target-depth fallback); a centered cursor preserves the centered case. Cover no hit and finite near-plane behavior.
3. Settings off restores the existing pivot/dolly path; test persistence through isolated App Group settings rather than UserDefaults.standard.

### TDD verification
Focused command: `./scripts/dev.sh test -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/MetalCameraTests` (reuse/extend an existing suite if appropriate; confirm tests are discovered and executed, not zero tests). After green run `./scripts/dev.sh test` including unchanged pixel references. Use hand-computed expectations/independent Khronos output for renderer math, not values copied from the implementation.

For UI assertions prefer deterministic in-process hosted components and background AX selection; visual checks must inspect the actual rendered result. These instructions supersede older generic launch/uitest directions in this description: background only, no focus steal, no `--snapshot`, no leftover Export sheets; XCUITest requires explicit approval for that run. No app launch is required for this backlog edit.

## Executable TDD baseline — 2026-11-04

**DEFINED; no executable behavioral red yet.**

No selection-retarget/cursor-ray input or settings seam exists. Current camera tests cover established Khronos orbit math only. Introduce the explicit retarget/dolly interface and then the defined independent camera assertions before its behavior.

Do not label this leaf test-ready until its defined cases compile, execute and fail on behavior. Interface/build errors are not feature-red evidence.

Authoritative baseline: `.atelier/tasks/ew2ifr55/baseline.md` in the primary checkout. Tests live in `/Users/mattias/dev/glb-preview/.worktrees/tdd-backlog-tests` (`codex/tdd-backlog-tests`) to preserve deliberate failures independently of active main-checkout implementation. Full run: `./scripts/dev.sh test`, exit 65; 178 tests in 40 suites; 10 failing new test functions plus the existing feature-reference test, 14 total issues (11 new assertions and 3 reference issues). Khronos sample references pass; the existing selection/all-overlays feature references fail with missing selection AABBs. References were not modified. Log: `.atelier/tasks/ew2ifr55/proof/isolated-full-test.log`; exact stable source hashes: `.atelier/tasks/ew2ifr55/proof/baseline-isolated.json`; archived tests: `.atelier/tasks/ew2ifr55/tests/`. Baseline HEAD `dbc169fc21a23d4ca63e6a32c3d11001ca60f302` plus the captured uncommitted source snapshot. Earlier AX-harness failures/zero-test runs are excluded. No feature task lifecycle is changed by this evidence edit.

name: EXP-015: Full-RGBA Metal/LowLevelTexture upload (keep mips)
description:
## Rank
1

## Classification
NEW

## Hypothesis
I believe `channels == .all` raster textures dominate residual load on 09/10 because each PNG/JPEG still pays `TextureResource.generate(from: CGImage)` (default `mipmapsMode: .allocateAndGenerateAll`), while KTX2 already uploads via Metal `LowLevelTexture` blit; routing full-RGBA maps through `MTKTextureLoader` (with `.generateMipmaps`) → existing LowLevel blit → `TextureResource(from:)` should cut 09/10 without touching scalar-channel swizzle (EXP-010 REJECT) and without dropping mips (`mipmapsMode.none` would fight corpus `LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR` samplers).

## Parent champion
cp-001 (`1329a23`, `sum_median_total_ms=7620.2`)

## Focus lane
C — textures · materials · scene · still

## Research basis
- Residual: cp-001 per-asset medians — 10 ≈ 2956 ms, 09 ≈ 2029 ms (≈65% of 7620); 10 ≈ 428 MPix / 57 images, 09 ≈ 183 MPix / 61 images (PNG IHDR scan of frozen corpus).
- Code: `RealityKitResourceContext.textureResource` — KTX2 uses `LowLevelTexture` + blit; raster falls through to `TextureResource.generate(from:options: CreateOptions(semantic:))` ([TextureResource.generate](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/textureresource/generate(from:withname:options:)); [CreateOptions](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/textureresource/createoptions) defaults `mipmapsMode` to `.allocateAndGenerateAll`).
- Samplers on 09/10/07/04: single sampler `minFilter=9987` (`LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR`) — so deleted idea `mipmapsMode: .none` is **not** best here (fidelity/shimmer risk; Apple forums contrast [.none vs allocateAndGenerateAll](https://developer.apple.com/forums/tags/realitykit)).
- Prefer Metal upload that **keeps mips**: [MTKTextureLoader.Option.generateMipmaps](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalkit/mtktextureloader/option/generatemipmaps) + same [LowLevelTexture](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/lowleveltexture) / [TextureResource(from:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/textureresource/init(from:)) pattern already used for KTX2; community MTL→RealityKit via LowLevel blit ([Apple Forums](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/799886)).
- **Not EXP-010:** that cached BGRA + **scalar ColorMask swizzle** and slowed mecha (+429 ms). This EXP is `.all` only; leave `singleChannelImage` / vImage path unchanged.
- Still path is small (~50 ms on 10) — not the lever.

## Approach
One change: when `channels == .all` and image is not KTX2, build `MTLTexture` from cached `CGImage` via `MTKTextureLoader` with mip generation enabled (semantic/sRGB matching `.color`/`.normal` as today), blit into `LowLevelTexture`, `TextureResource(from:)`, cache by image id + `.all` as today. Fallback to current `TextureResource.generate` on upload failure. Do not alter scalar extracts or sampler descriptors.

## Likely files
- `Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift`
- `GLBPreviewTests/Texture*.swift` if new upload path needs coverage

## Done when
- Bench vs cp-001 / recorded_control `1329a23`; win must concentrate on 09/10 (and maybe 04/08), not net-regress mecha like EXP-010.
- 0/10 load errors; stills match control on baseColor/normal for a textured asset (mips present — no intentional shimmer from `.none`).
- No scalar-swizzle / EXP-008 ARGB / EXP-012 UV changes.

## Forbidden
- Retry EXP-010 LowLevelTexture **channel swizzle** / scalar Metal path without new evidence.
- EXP-008 ARGB sibling cache; EXP-012 UV fuse.
- Blind `mipmapsMode: .none` (quality cut vs corpus mip samplers; sibling/deleted idea).
- Prepare skip; anim disable; lane A/B work.
result: Decision REJECT. Candidate 8066.8 vs recorded_control 7620.2 (+447 ms / +5.9%, beyond noise). 0/10 errors; 9/10 slower; hypothesized 09/10 wins inverted (+55 / +190). Worktree+branch discarded. Artifacts: experiments/results/EXP-015.json

name: Write engine seam adapters
description:
## Why

The heart of the cutover. Thin conformances so PreviewUI views stay untouched. Work only in
`/Users/mattias/dev/glb-preview/.worktrees/ui` on `ui-rebuild`.

## Step 0 — PREREQUISITE (do this first, or nothing compiles)

`PreviewUI/` is **not** in the `GLBPreview` target's `sources` today — only the `PreviewUIShell`
target compiles it (`project.yml`). So `SceneModel`, `ViewportController`, etc. are **not in scope**
for the app target, and `EngineSceneModel: SceneModel` will fail with *"cannot find type 'SceneModel'
in scope."*

Fix before writing any adapter:
1. In `project.yml`, add `- PreviewUI` to the `GLBPreview` target's `sources` list (alongside
   `- GLBPreview`, `- path: Shared`, …).
2. `xcodegen generate`.
3. `xcodebuild -scheme GLBPreview … build` still succeeds (PreviewUI is generic, imports no
   `Shared/`; it just now also compiles into the app target). Old `HostOutlinerView` etc. still
   exist — no conflict; deletion happens later in `vfcn76gm`.

`PreviewUI/Seam/AppDefaultsStore.swift` lives in PreviewUI, so it is now available to the app too.

## Scope

New folder `GLBPreview/Engine/`. Map existing engine types to the seam; **no PreviewUI rewrites**,
**no engine changes** beyond what the honesty task (`g21akn5r`, done) already landed.

**Read the current seam signatures before implementing — they grew in Part A:**
`PreviewUI/Seam/SceneModel.swift`, `Availability.swift`, `ViewportController.swift` (now has
`activeSceneID`/`setScene`, `selectedMaterialVariantIndex`/`setMaterialVariant`, `screenshot()`),
`SelectionModel.swift`, `SettingsStore.swift` + `AppDefaultsStore.swift`,
`AnimationPlaybackController.swift`, and `Models.swift` (value types).

Stateful protocols (`ViewportController`, `SelectionModel`, `SettingsStore`,
`AnimationPlaybackController`) are `@MainActor`, `AnyObject`, `Observable` → adapters are
`@MainActor @Observable final class`. `SceneModel`/`Availability` are `Sendable` value snapshots →
`EngineSceneModel` is a **struct** rebuilt from the document.

| Adapter | Wraps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `EngineSceneModel` (struct) | `GLTFSessionDocument` + `PreviewStats` + `ModelDimensions` + `GLTFValidationState` + `PipelineReport` | Build `nodeTree` from flat `document.nodes` child indices; radians→degrees for fov/cones. Materials already carry `workflow`/`alphaMode`/`isDoubleSided` + factors + bound `materialIndices` (g21akn5r). `materialVariantNames` from host variant list. **Validation is async** (nil while pending; `.success`/`.failed`/`.skipped` after first paint): rebuild the struct when it resolves so the inspector updates; map `.failed`/`.skipped` to a synthetic info `ValidationResult.Issue`, never silence. |
| `EngineViewportController` | session state + `PreviewCamera` + `FocusedPreviewCommands` + still path | `screenshot()` wraps `ContentView.screenshotCurrentCameraPose` — it is **private** at `ContentView.swift:294`; extract to a shared helper or wrap. Not a framebuffer grab. Lighting: degrees↔radians; `usesFileLights` ↔ host dim-studio/file-lights; do **not** fight `AppLook.useEnvironmentMap`. `setScene`/`setMaterialVariant` drive the host re-convert (lives in `HostSidebarModel` until B1). |
| `EngineSelectionModel` | `HostSidebarModel` (`selectNode`/`isolate` **toggle**, `HostSidebarModel.swift:38,44`) + `PreviewSelectionVisuals` + `SelectionDetail` | Seam `select(_:)`/`isolate(_:)` are **set-with-nil-to-clear**; host toggles. Reconcile at the boundary (call host toggle only when the new value differs). `isVisible(_:)` derives from `hide` + `soloHides`. `detail` → `NodeDetail` via `SelectionDetail.resolve`. |
| `Availability` | `DerivedAvailability<EngineSceneModel>` (already written) | Feed channels from `EntityLoader.LoadedModel.debugModes` (`EntityLoader.swift:11`, populated via `PreviewDebugMode.available(from: json)` at load). Do **not** persist raw JSON on `GLTFSessionDocument`. |
| `AnimationPlaybackController` | `PreviewScene` clock + `PreviewClip` | Read the protocol in `PreviewUI/Seam/AnimationPlaybackController.swift` for exact members. The RealityKit clock may **no-op `advance`** (the engine advances itself). |
| `EngineSettingsStore` | host `SettingsKeys` **and** `AppLook`/`AppLookStore` | See "Settings mapping" below — this is two storage backends, not one. |

## Settings mapping (do not miss — the IBL picker breaks silently otherwise)

The seam `SettingKey` names already match the host `UserDefaults` keys for the canvas defaults, so
those are a pass-through:

- `autoRotate`, `showFloor`, `showPills` (= host `settings.preview.showToolbar`), `backdrop`
  (= `settings.preview.background`), `appearance`, `projection`, `center` → `UserDefaults`
  (via `AppDefaultsStore`). `center`/`projection` stay **session-only** — no app-default write.
- **Environment keys have NO host UserDefaults key** — map them to `AppLook`/`AppLookStore`
  (`Shared/AppLook.swift`): `useEnvironmentMap` ↔ `AppLook.useEnvironmentMap`, `environmentCatalog`
  ↔ `AppLook.catalogRaw`, `customEnvironmentFile` ↔ `AppLook.customFileName`; write via
  `AppLookStore.apply(_:)`. Reading/writing these through plain `UserDefaults` would leave the
  Settings IBL picker driving nothing.
- `appearance` must apply app-wide (`SettingsAppearance.apply`) — that wiring is the injection
  task's job; the store just persists the value.

Implement the per-window lazy overlay (A3c) on `AppDefaultsStore` exactly as `MockSettings` does
(no eager seed; untouched keys track the observed default). **Do not** stop `ContentView`'s
seed-once here — that host swap belongs to the injection task `j3yvbupw`.

## Tests (use the committed fixtures via `GLBPreviewTests/TestFixtures.swift`)

`EntityLoader.load` a fixture, build the adapter, assert the mapping. The adaptive-UI fixtures prove
`Availability` cheaply:

- `.cube` / `.tiny` → plain: no anim/lights/cameras/skin/morph; single scene.
- `.boxAnimated` → `hasAnimations`, playback clips non-empty.
- `.lights` → `hasLights`; `.cameras` → `hasCameras`; `.multiScene` → `isMultiScene`;
  `.rigged` → `hasSkin`; `.morph` → `hasMorphs`; `.missingChannels` → shorter
  `availableDebugChannels` + material chips omit absent maps.
- `.invalid` → validation issues surface; `.offcenter` → `dimensions.authoredOrigin != .zero`.

No `--snapshot`/flatten harness (AGENTS.md §6). This task adds no live window — that is `j3yvbupw`.

## Subtasks (this is the shared context; do the subtasks in order)

1. **Expose seam in the app target** (Step 0 above) — blocks the other three.
2. **Read-model adapters** — `EngineSceneModel` + `Availability` + `AnimationPlaybackController`.
3. **Control adapters** — `EngineViewportController` + `EngineSelectionModel`.
4. **Settings adapter** — `EngineSettingsStore` (UserDefaults overlay + AppLook mapping).

2–4 are parallel after 1 (disjoint files under `GLBPreview/Engine/`). This parent completes only
when all four are done. The tables and mapping notes above are the reference; each subtask restates
what it needs.

PreviewUI rewrites; no engine changes beyond g21akn5r.

name: EXP-010: LowLevelTexture swizzle for scalar channels
description:
## Rank
1 (best expected impact × confidence × simplicity post–EXP-009)

## Classification
NEW

## Hypothesis
I believe metallic/roughness/AO/specular scalar channels still pay full `vImageExtractChannel` + `TextureResource.generate(from: CGImage)` per (image, channel) on raster textures, while the KTX2 path already uploads once and applies `MTLTextureSwizzleChannels`. Routing non-KTX2 channel extracts through one Metal upload + swizzled LowLevelTexture should cut load time on texture-heavy corpus assets (especially 10-mecha ~57 images and 09-animals ~61) without changing visible fidelity.

## Parent champion
EXP-009

## Research basis (links)
- Local code: `Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift` — KTX2 branch already uses `LowLevelTexture` + `channels.textureSwizzle`; raster path uses `singleChannelImage` (`vImageExtractChannel_ARGB8888`) then `TextureResource.generate(from:)`.
- Apple: [MTLTextureSwizzleChannels](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtltextureswizzlechannels) — rearrange/duplicate sampled channels without copying texel buffers.
- Apple: [LowLevelTexture](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/lowleveltexture) / WWDC24 spatial drawing — create `TextureResource` from `LowLevelTexture`.
- Apple: [TextureResource.generate(from:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/textureresource/generate(from:withname:options:)) — synchronous CGImage → texture (costly when repeated per channel).
- Metal by Example (2019): texture swizzling avoids channel-duplication copies — https://metalbyexample.com/new-in-metal-3/
- Post-009 residual: mecha+animals ≈ 63% of champion sum (`experiments/results/EXP-009.json`); vegetation no longer dominant after opacity cut.

## Approach (one change)
Extend the existing KTX2-style path so that when `channels != .all` for a raster `GLTFImage`, upload the source once to Metal (or reuse a cached MTL/LowLevel texture), then create channel-specific `TextureResource`s via swizzle / texture view instead of `singleChannelImage` + `TextureResource.generate(from: gray CGImage)`. Keep the existing `(image.identifier, ColorMask)` cache. Do **not** reintroduce EXP-008’s ARGB vImage sibling-buffer cache.

## Likely files
- `Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift`
- Possibly tests under `GLBPreviewTests/TextureTests.swift`

## Done when
- Full corpus `LABEL=EXP-010` bench vs same-machine `EXP-010-champ` (or fresh EXP-009 control).
- KEEP only if beyond noise (~3% of champion sum) with concentration on texture-heavy assets (09/10), correctness intact (MR/AO/specular channel mapping unchanged).
- Ledgers updated; REJECT discards worktree.

## Forbidden / out of scope
- EXP-008 ARGB sibling-cache retry without new evidence
- Skipping textures, lowering resolution, changing corpus
- Shipping prepare skip / claiming prepare-path wins
- Parallel benches; merging to champion (Executor only implements + benches)
result:
## Decision
**REJECT**

## Hypothesis
Raster scalar channels (metallic/roughness/AO/specular) pay per-channel `vImageExtractChannel` + `TextureResource.generate`; routing through one Metal upload + `LowLevelTexture` swizzle (like KTX2) should cut load on texture-heavy 09/10.

## Implementation
- Worktree: `.worktrees/exp-010` on `exp/EXP-010`
- Changed `Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift`: cache BGRA `MTLTexture` per image UUID; scalar `ColorMask` builds swizzled `LowLevelTexture` + blit (shared helper with KTX2 path). Fallback to existing vImage path if upload fails.
- Commits (discarded with branch): `498fba4` swizzle path; `c986d88` fix DeviceRGB+premul-first CGContext (unsupported alpha-first caused first bench 8956).
- Did **not** redo EXP-008 ARGB sibling cache.

## Bench (serial, same machine)
| Label | sum_median_total_ms | sum_median_load_ms |
|-------|--------------------:|-------------------:|
| EXP-010-champ (main, champion code) | **8208.8** | 8026.8 |
| EXP-010 (candidate, fixed upload) | **8388.5** | 8187.4 |

- Δ vs same-machine control: **+179.7 ms (+2.19%)**
- Noise: 3% of frozen champ 7732 ≈ 232 ms; 3% of control ≈ 246 ms — |Δ| under noise but **wrong direction**
- 8/10 assets faster on mid sizes; **09 +35 ms / 10 +429 ms** — hypothesized concentration **failed** (mecha dominates regression)
- 0/10 load errors
- TextureChannelExtractTests + TextureAlphaUsageTests: pass

## Complexity

## Ledgers
- `experiments/results/EXP-010.json`, `EXP-010-champ.json`
- `experiments/WHAT-WE-TRIED.md` + `experiments/results.json` entry

name: Write the go/no-go and decide what happens to the spike branch
description:
## Why

The spike's output is a decision, not code. Without this written down, the next session re-derives it or, worse, re-runs it.

## Approach

Write `docs/decision-web-renderer.md` in the worktree covering:

1. **The question.** Can one renderer serve Finder thumbnail, Quick Look and the document window, given that renderer must be WebKit for fidelity reasons?
2. **What was measured**, with numbers — the benchmark table from the originating session plus this spike's Finder timings.
3. **The answer**, go or no-go, and the evidence.
4. **If go:** what the migration actually costs. `PreviewUI/` (8,611 lines) is untouched — it imports only SwiftUI/Foundation/Observation/AppKit and reaches the renderer through `ViewportController` and `SceneModel`. `Shared/Convert/` (2,713) and the prepare stage (802) are deleted. The real cost is that a large share of 5,491 test lines assert on converted RealityKit entities and have no Swift home afterwards; the honest replacement is pixel-diffing against the Khronos sample set.
5. **If no-go:** amend `AGENTS.md`. Today it states the goal as "closest practical 1:1 glTF **via native RealityKit**" — two halves in tension. A no-go means the RealityKit half wins and the ceiling should be written down explicitly, so nobody keeps chasing 1:1.

## Follow-up tasks to create (do not do them here)

- **If go:** a separate epic for the migration, first task being the production renderer choice (Khronos Sample Renderer vs three.js) — that decision was deliberately excluded from this spike and must not be inherited from it by default.
- **If no-go:** a task to surface the ceiling in the app's own honesty UI, so a user inspecting a transmission or iridescence asset is told our renderer cannot show it rather than being shown a plausible-looking wrong image. This matters more given the product goal is pre-flight checking for web 3D.

## Branch disposition

Per `AGENTS.md`, before `git worktree remove`: run `git log main..spike/web-thumbnail` and cherry-pick anything worth keeping. `.worktrees/` is gitignored and deleting it loses the work permanently.

Keep the branch either way — even on a no-go, a working `WebStillRenderer` plus recorded sandbox denials is what stops this question being reopened from scratch in six months.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/decision-web-renderer.md` committed on the spike branch, with real numbers and a stated verdict.
- Follow-up dex tasks created for whichever branch of the decision applies.
- Repo root working tree still shows exactly the 12 modified + 1 untracked files it started with.
result:
## Done

`docs/decision-web-renderer.md` committed on `spike/web-thumbnail` as `3ca637c`. Verdict **GO**, with the single entitlement, the measured timings from both stacks, the migration cost breakdown, the traps that produced false positives, and an explicit "what is not proven" section.

## Follow-ups created

- **`3ejklvvg` — Migrate rendering from RealityKit to WebKit.** Carries the six-step shape, the test-coverage cost, and the three known unknowns (notarization, folder-scale thumbnail throughput, Quick Look preview never attempted).
- **`w5m5lvzg` — Choose the production web renderer** (child). Records that three.js was a spike convenience and must not be inherited by default, the case for the Khronos Sample Renderer, and five checks to answer from a running prototype rather than documentation.

The no-go follow-up was not created: the spike returned GO.

## Branch disposition

`spike/web-thumbnail` kept, four commits ahead of `3d2b374`:

```
3ca637c Record the renderer decision and the spike evidence
347c390 Grant the thumbnail extension network client access for WKWebView
de1188f Route thumbnails through the WebGL renderer behind a defaults flag
adcab0c Add off-screen WebGL still renderer for the thumbnail spike
```

Worktree at `.worktrees/web-thumb-spike` left in place. `WebStillRenderer` plus the recorded entitlement finding are what stop this question being reopened from scratch; do not `git worktree remove` without merging or cherry-picking first — `.worktrees/` is gitignored and deleting it loses the branch content.

Nothing merged to `main`. `main` still ships RealityKit.

## Correction recorded

Partway through this subtask the decision document was committed to **`main`** instead of the spike branch — a `cd` to the repo root from an earlier dex invocation persisted, and the branch was not re-checked before `git add -A`. That commit swept up the user's 12 uncommitted work-in-progress files.

Undone with `git reset --mixed 3d2b374`. Verified restored byte-for-byte: 12 modified tracked files, `12 files changed, 522 insertions(+), 496 deletions(-)` matching the pre-spike diffstat exactly, and `Shared/PreviewSession.swift` untracked at 48 lines. The document was then committed on `spike/web-thumbnail` where it belongs.

> Lesson for the next agent: `.dex/` exists only in the repo root, so dex commands need `cd /Users/mattias/dev/glb-preview` — and that `cd` persists in this shell. Use a subshell, `(cd /Users/mattias/dev/glb-preview && dex ...)`, or check `git branch --show-current` before every commit.

name: EXP-019: Skip TextureResource mipgen (mipmapsMode.none)
description:
## Rank
impact×confidence×simplicity: **high × medium-high × high** — after EXP-017 KEEP (−554 ms on 06/07/08), residual is texture-heavy 09+10 (~4985 ms / 65% of cp-001 sum). Sync `TextureResource.generate` still uses CreateOptions default `.allocateAndGenerateAll` for every raster (61+57 images; mecha also doubles MR into green+blue generates). One-line options change; fewest files.

## Classification
NEW

## Hypothesis
I believe load on 09/10 is dominated by **accidental full mip-chain generation** on the convert hot path: `TextureResource.CreateOptions(semantic:)` defaults to `mipmapsMode: .allocateAndGenerateAll`, so every `TextureResource.generate(from: CGImage)` allocates and fills a full pyramid (~+33% texels + CPU/GPU mipgen) even though preview/still framing is close and samples level 0. Setting `mipmapsMode: .none` keeps **full-resolution base textures** (bench still stays fully textured; not a progressive/first-paint skip) while removing derived mip work that is not required for correctness of load+still.

## Parent champion
cp-001 (`1329a23`, sum_median_total_ms=7620.179249000001)

## Focus lane
FULL PIPELINE AUDIT → textures (lane C residual after EXP-017 mesh KEEP / EXP-018 concurrency REJECT)

## Research basis (concrete + links)
- Call graph (bench): `LoadTimeBenchTests` → `EntityLoader.load` → `prepareGLB` / `GLTFAsset(url:)` → `MainActor` `RealityKitConvert.convert` → per-material `RealityKitResourceContext.textureResource` → sync `TextureResource.generate(from:options:)` → then `StillRenderer.capture` (render ≪ load; IBL cached).
- Local: `Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift` — `CreateOptions(semantic: semantic)` with **no** mipmapsMode override; opacity path same default.
- SDK default: CreateOptions.init(semantic:mipmapsMode: = .allocateAndGenerateAll).
- Apple: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/realitykit/textureresource/mipmapsmode
- Corpus: all v2 textured assets use sampler minFilter LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR; 09=61 / 10=57 images.
- Contrast: EXP-015 still generated mips via Metal (+447 ms); EXP-018 concurrent prefetch forbade mipmapsMode:.none and regressed (+562 ms). This isolates the deferred mip lever only.

## Approach (one change)
In RealityKitResourceContext.textureResource (and opacityTexture CreateOptions), pass TextureResource.CreateOptions(semantic:semantic, mipmapsMode:.none). Leave KTX2 LowLevel blit unchanged. No concurrency, no resolution downscale, no channel/swizzle changes.

## Likely files
- Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift (~2 call sites)

## Done when
- LABEL=EXP-019 full corpus-v2 vs cp-001 @ 1329a23
- KEEP if beyond ~3% (~229 ms) or ≥8/10 same direction; expect 09/10 concentration; 0/10 errors
- Still fully textured at base resolution

## Forbidden
- Resolution/channel/compression cuts; skipping required maps
- Retry EXP-018 concurrency, EXP-015 MTK/LowLevel, EXP-008/010
- prepare-skip; includeAnimations: false; corpus special-case; v1-as-v2
- Claiming identical zoomed-out mip filtering (gate is load+still base fidelity)
result: REJECT EXP-019: sum_median_total 7516.1 vs SM control 7620.2 (−104 ms / −1.37%, inside ~229 ms 3% noise); 6/10 faster (09 −39 / 10 −97; 08 +42). 0/10 errors; base textures retained. Worktree+branch removed. accepted_queue unchanged (EXP-017 only).

name: Seam 4: spike framework resources read from appex

name: EXP-024: fused UV float2 decode (skip multi-pass bake)
description:
## Rank
high residual on proven mesh-bound 06/07/08 (~2.6M UVs); med-high confidence; few files.

## Classification
NEW (UV-specific fused accessor decode). Not a retry of EXP-014 (general float*→SIMD) or EXP-021 (index stream). Related to but not identical to REJECT EXP-012 (fused wrap+V-flip on MeshBuffers path without LowLevelMesh UV write).

## Hypothesis
bakedTextureCoordinates still pays GLTFPackedDataForAccessor + SIMD2 build + full-span wrapSingleTile min/max scan + V-flip map on every TEXCOORD before MeshBuffers / EXP-017 LowLevelMesh memcpy. On corpus 06/07/08 that is ~2.6M float2s (~21MB) with up to five passes. A single bufferView→float2 path with fused RealityKit V-flip (and wrap only when accessor min/max leave the unit tile) should cut convert beyond noise on those assets.

## Parent champion
Was cp-001; after in-flight checkpoint tip will be EXP-017 integrate @ 1aceeda (packed LowLevelMesh). Bench vs post-checkpoint recorded_control when available; if pre-checkpoint, control = EXP-017 KEEP 7066.1.

## Focus lane
B — parse · accessors · decode

## Research basis
- WWDC24 LowLevelMesh: https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2024/10104/
- LowLevelMesh docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/RealityKit/LowLevelMesh
- Corpus: 06/07/08 TEXCOORD_0 tight FLOAT VEC2 stride 8; EXP-017 memcpy pos/norm/tan but still calls bakedTextureCoordinates
- EXP-017 KEEP −554 ms on 06/07/08; UV residual remains
- EXP-014 / EXP-021 REJECT — do not broaden to POSITION/NORMAL or indices
- EXP-012 REJECT fused wrap+flip — this is decode→LowLevelMesh UV write, not the same MeshBuffers UV fuse

## Approach (one change)
Replace multi-pass bakedTextureCoordinates with one fused tight-float2 decode: read bufferView floats once, apply wrap only when needed (prefer accessor min/max gate), fuse V-flip. When EXP-017 packed UV buffer exists, write bytes straight into LowLevelMesh UV buffer (no [SIMD2<Float>] intermediate). Keep transform-matrix path when KHR_texture_transform is present.

## Likely files
- Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Mesh.swift
- optionally Shared/TextureUV.swift / Shared/PackedAccessors.swift

## Done when
LABEL=EXP-024 bench vs same-machine post-checkpoint control; KEEP only beyond noise_rule or ≥8/10; TextureUV/convert tests green.

## Forbidden
index streaming (EXP-021); EXP-014 retry for POSITION/NORMAL/TANGENT; blind EXP-012 retry; quality cuts; skip required wrap/V-flip/transform; prepare-skip; corpus special-case; v1-as-v2; lanes A/C work.
result: REJECT +98.5 ms (+1.34%) vs cp-002 7372.9; under ~221 ms noise; 3/10 faster (06/07/08 helped, 09/10 regress). Worktree discarded.

name: EXP-031: MR map single-upload + MaterialParameters.Texture.swizzle
description:
## Rank
residual_share(10=42.9% texture_ms≈2937; MR dual ≈43% of 10 MP-generates) × evidence(macOS 15 MaterialParameters.Texture.swizzle; SceneKit textureComponents pattern; EXP-010 was LowLevel blit not this API) × simplicity(one material/context path; delete dual vImage+generate) — prefer delete over alternate upload.

## Classification
NEW (not EXP-010 VARIANT: no Metal/LowLevel blit; material-layer swizzle on one TextureResource.generate)

## Hypothesis
On 10-bot_mecha_warrior, each of 16 metallicRoughness maps pays two full-res TextureResource.generate calls (G→gray + B→gray; ~117 MP ×2). Use one TextureResource per metallicRoughnessTexture as .all/.raw + macOS 15 MaterialParameters.Texture.swizzle G→R / B→R instead of dual vImage + dual generate (RealityKit scalar samples R), deleting the second generate and both vImage extracts — enough on (10, texture_ms) to clear ~224 ms noise (est. ~half of ~1.3 s MR share).

## Parent champion
cp-003 / 173fc71f3e366dc26b8323d98ccecc228a16c8b5 / 7464.8 ms (noise ~224 ms)

## Focus lane
C (textures·materials·scene·still)

## Residual cell
**(10-bot_mecha_warrior, texture_ms)** — primary; secondary 07 if its one MR map moves same direction. 09 has no MR textures (SG diffuse-only) so must not be the sole win story.

## Research basis
- residual-map cp-003: 10 share 42.9%, texture_ms 2937; 09 29.5%/1833 (no MR dual)
- Asset anatomy 10: 16× MR (2048–4096), metallicFactor=0 on only 1 mat; G/B both spatially varying → cannot skip maps; 0 byte-identical image dups
- MP split 10: .all maps ~310 MP once vs MR ~117 MP ×2 generates (~43% of generate work)
- SDK: MaterialParameters.Texture.swizzle: MTLTextureSwizzleChannels (macOS 15+); CustomMaterial has init(resource, swizzle)
- SceneKit/glTF loaders use textureComponents = .green/.blue on one shared texture
- EXP-010 REJECT was CPU→MTLTexture + LowLevel blit swizzle (+429 ms on 10) — different mechanism; this keeps TextureResource.generate once

## Approach (one change)
For metallicRoughnessTexture only: resolve one TextureResource via existing raster path with channels: .all, semantic: .raw (cache as .all); wrap into roughness/metallic PhysicallyBasedMaterial.Texture with sampler + swizzle mapping green→R and blue→R (or RGB=.green/.blue). Do not vImage-extract or generate per-channel resources for this slot. Leave baseColor/normal/emissive/AO/KTX2 paths unchanged. Fallback to today’s green/blue extract if swizzle unavailable.

## Likely files
- Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Material.swift
- Shared/Convert/RealityKitResourceContext.swift (helper to build swizzled Texture; optional)
- GLBPreviewTests/TextureTests.swift (swizzle / MR bind smoke)

## Done when
LABEL=EXP-031 ./scripts/load-bench.sh vs cp-003 control; KEEP iff beyond ~3% noise (~224 ms) with honest concentration on **10 texture_ms** (dual MR delete); else REJECT. Full-res, default CreateOptions, no Metal blit upload path.

## Forbidden
CreateOptions* (019/022/027); EXP-010 Metal/LowLevel scalar blit; EXP-015/018; EXP-030 ImageIO path; quality cuts; downsample; fused UV (012/024); ASTC; corpus special-case; changing 09 SG/prepare path.
result: REJECT (+9376.8 ms / +125.6% vs cp-003 7464.8). Tweak1 G→Y/B→A 16bpp pack (424494a) after NEAR_MISS −191 ms @ 2b0e992; inverted residual 10 +9302 (5/5 reps ~12s) / 09 +61. Must-not-retry: MR swizzle / gray+alpha 16bpp pack dual-delete. Worktree+branch removed. reject_only_batches=2. User stop — no further research.

description:
**Why:** the user-facing timeline.
**Scope:** design-system glass HUD component (e.g. `DSTimeline` in `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/Components/Glass/`) placed along the canvas bottom between the gizmo and the dimensions readout, shown only when the file has a clip with duration > 0: play/pause button (Space shortcut while canvas focused), scrubber with time readout (mm:ss.ff / duration), clip picker (All + each clip), loop toggle, speed menu. Selecting an Animations row in the layer list selects that clip. Rows targeted by the active clips get a small "animated" indicator via `DSOutlineRow`. Morph inspector shows live weights.
**Done when / Verification:** UI test: play advances time, scrub changes the pose; on-screen screenshots light/dark; `./scripts/dev.sh test` + `uitest`.

**Spec:** `.agents/plans/2026-11-04-scene-interaction.md` (coverage table + decisions log). Read `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md` first.
**Rules:** work on `main` unless told otherwise; never regenerate pixel references for a default render (`TestModels/References/`); new UI goes through `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/` components; check UI on screen yourself (`./scripts/dev.sh run <fixture>`, `screencapture`), never ask the user to test.

## TDD execution contract
- The cases below are defined test contracts, not implemented tests or observed failures. Baseline: **not run for this backlog edit**. Use existing suites where they cover the behavior; proposed suite names are destinations, not existing files.
- **Red first:** after prerequisites are available, add the smallest deterministic behavioral test before its production change. Run the focused suite and record test name, command, revision/worktree state, actual failing assertion and log path. A missing API/compiler error may guide initial scaffolding, but establish a compiling behavioral failure before implementation; build/tool/fixture errors are not feature-red evidence. Never use unconditional failures, skip/expected-failure markers, or loosen an oracle to manufacture red.
- **Green, then refactor:** implement only enough to pass that test, run the remaining cases, then refactor with tests green. Blocked leaves define tests now and establish executable red after their prerequisite lands; do not invent placeholder dependencies.
- For already implemented behavior, keep the regression green and, where safe, prove sensitivity using a temporary isolated mutation/reversion of only that behavior. Do not undo another worker's edits or claim retroactive red. Record unavailable red evidence honestly.
- **Completion evidence:** case → test/fixture → observed red (or documented existing-behavior exception) → green, with commands and log paths in the result. Passing tests alone do not prove this contract was followed.

### Defined tests (write before production changes)
1. Host the HUD with an injected playback controller: no/zero-duration clips hide it; Play/Pause toggles state; scrubber changes time and evaluated pose with a deterministic clock.
2. Loop/speed/clip controls update controller state; selecting an animation row selects its clip; active-target indicators and morph weight readouts update.
3. Space acts only with canvas focus, not while editing text. Capture light/dark hosted states for visual review; avoid elapsed-wall-clock sleeps.

### TDD verification
Focused command: `./scripts/dev.sh test -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/TimelineHUDTests` (reuse/extend an existing suite if appropriate; confirm tests are discovered and executed, not zero tests). After green run `./scripts/dev.sh test` including unchanged pixel references. Use hand-computed expectations/independent Khronos output for renderer math, not values copied from the implementation.

For UI assertions prefer deterministic in-process hosted components and background AX selection; visual checks must inspect the actual rendered result. These instructions supersede older generic launch/uitest directions in this description: background only, no focus steal, no `--snapshot`, no leftover Export sheets; XCUITest requires explicit approval for that run. No app launch is required for this backlog edit.

## Executable TDD baseline — 2026-11-04

**RED (initial visibility) — measured coverage, not task completion.**

`GLTFInspectorTests/SceneInteractionComponentTests.swift`: animatedFileOffersPlaybackControls fails: a loaded BoxAnimated fixture with duration > 0 exposes no Play control. staticFileDoesNotOfferPlaybackControls passes. Play/pause/scrub/speed behavior awaits bi329hbl; this is not full HUD coverage.

Focused reproduction: `cd /Users/mattias/dev/glb-preview/.worktrees/tdd-backlog-tests && ./scripts/dev.sh test -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/SceneInteractionComponentTests`. Confirm nonzero executed test count. Remaining cases in this task still apply.

name: Port Settings panes and lazy overlay
description:
## Why

Shell `SettingKey`s are five canvas keys. The real app's three Settings panes (especially IBL/AppLook) must not be lost. Eager session seed also kills live default-tracking (P34).

## Scope

Primarily `PreviewUI/Seam/SettingsStore.swift`, `PreviewUIShell/Mocks/MockSettings.swift`, shell Settings UI. Re-home existing `AppLook` / `KhronosEnvironments` / import UI — do not rewrite IBL behavior.

- Expand `SettingKey` for real ports only: appearance, showPills←`showToolbar`, useEnvironmentMap, environmentCatalog, customEnvironmentFile.
- Drop `.center` / `.projection` from the persisted default set (session-only; center on, perspective).
- Stop `seedSessionFromDefaultsIfNeeded`. A window overrides a key only when the user changes that control.
- Shared app-level `@Observable` defaults store (UserDefaults + `didChangeNotification`) injected into every window. Settings scene writes that store.
- Rebuild 3-tab Settings (General / Preview / About): appearance, default-app, canvas defaults, IBL catalog + custom HDR/EXR, About + keep Sparkle on the app menu.
- Do **not** add `autoPlay`.
- Out of scope: engine adapters; changing `PreviewLighting` algorithm; host ContentView seed-once (that dies in the adapter task).

## Done when

- Shell Settings has three panes; IBL picker still works against mocks/AppLook.
- Two windows: change a default → window still on default updates live; window that overrode that key does not.
- `clearSession()` re-tracks defaults.
- `PreviewUIShell` builds.

## Handoff

Key names; which type owns the shared defaults store; leftover host seed-once location for adapters.
result:
## What changed

`AppDefaultsStore` is the shared UserDefaults + `didChangeNotification` store. `MockSettings` is a lazy session overlay (no `seedSessionFromDefaultsIfNeeded`). Center/projection stay session-only and are not registered as app defaults. Settings is three tabs (General / Preview / About) with appearance, canvas defaults, IBL catalog keys, custom HDR/EXR filename, About. Shell open path reads defaults without pinning.

## Files changed

`PreviewUI/Seam/AppDefaultsStore.swift`, `SettingsStore.swift`, `PreviewUI/Settings/PreviewSettingsRoot.swift`, `PreviewUIShell/Mocks/MockSettings.swift`, `ShellDefaultsView.swift`, `ShellWindow.swift`, `PreviewUIShellApp.swift`, `SettingsLiveProof.swift`

## Commands run

- `xcodebuild -scheme PreviewUIShell … build` → BUILD SUCCEEDED
- `PreviewUIShell --proof-cutover-a` → PASS (lazy overlay: tracking window follows default; override stays; `clearSession` re-tracks)

## Verification

Two `MockSettings` on one `AppDefaultsStore` prove live default tracking vs override isolation.

## Browser observations

N/A

## Remaining risks or follow-ups

Host `ContentView` seed-once and `AppLookStore` still own the real IBL file until B1. Shell Settings writes `SettingKey`s (`useEnvironmentMap` / `environmentCatalog` / `customEnvironmentFile`); adapter maps those onto `AppLook`. Default-app control only shows for `com.laurie.GLBPreview`. Sparkle stays on the host app menu.

## Next recommended task

`mhapkvgf` Write engine seam adapters

name: EXP-016: convert-time metalRough skips bake-gated rewrite
description:
Rank: 1 (lane A)
Classification: VARIANT (cheaper-prepare; lineage EXP-004)
Hypothesis: On prepare-hit 09 (67 factor-only KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness mats, 61 images → bake gated, RealityPrepare false), EntityLoader still full-parses/serializes/writes ~208MB solely to remap JSON factors. Applying the same metalRoughFrom factor mapping at RealityKitConvert from GLTFKit2.specularGlossiness and short-circuiting prepareGLB when bake is gated and RealityPrepare is not needed removes that I/O without skipping conversion.
Parent champion: cp-001 (7620.2 ms, tip 1329a23)
Focus lane: A (I/O · prepare · EntityLoader)
Research basis:
- Asset 09 probe: 67 SG / 0 sgTex / 61 images / 0 integer accessors → MetalRoughPrepare only, shouldBakeTextures=false, RealityPrepare=false
- EXP-013 JSON+BIN splice still rewrote ~208MB temp → 09 +18.5 ms; EXP-005-v2 GLTFAsset(data:) prepare-hit ~+8 ms → rewrite I/O dominates residual prepare, not URL vs Data
- EXP-004 allowed cheaper-prepare VARIANT (not skip-required)
- Don McCurdy / glTF-Transform metalRough + archived KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness: https://www.donmccurdy.com/2022/11/28/converting-gltf-pbr-materials-from-specgloss-to-metalrough/
- Khronos conversion: https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/tree/main/extensions/2.0/Archived/KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness
- GLTFKit2 already exposes specularGlossiness (PreviewEmissive uses it); convert currently ignores it
Approach (one change): In prepareGLB, when MetalRoughPrepare.needsConversion && !shouldBakeTextures && !RealityPrepare.needsPrepare, return original URL; in RealityKitConvert+Material, if specularGlossiness is present, apply existing MetalRoughPrepare factor formulas (baseColor/metallic/roughness + specularColor) using diffuseTexture as baseColorTexture—same fidelity as today's rewrite path for factor-only assets.
Likely files: Shared/EntityLoader.swift, Shared/Convert/RealityKitConvert+Material.swift, Shared/MetalRoughPrepare.swift (expose gate + factor helper)
Done when: LABEL=EXP-016 load-bench vs recorded_control; prefer 09-concentrated win; |delta|≥3% (~229ms) or ≥8/10 same direction; SpecGlossTests + LoaderMaterialTests still pass; bake-needed / RealityPrepare assets still rewrite.
Forbidden: prepare-skip without convert-time mapping; quality cuts; corpus id special-case; prepare-skip for bake/RealityPrepare paths; EXP-013 BIN splice retry; GLTFAsset(data:) retry without new evidence.
result: REJECT −187 ms (−2.46%) SM vs cp-001 control 7620.2; 7/10 under ~229ms noise. Worktree discarded.

name: Light gizmos: sun plate + line, point diamond, spot cone
description:
**Why:** see where `KHR_lights_punctual` lights are, what type they are and where they point.

Reference look (user screenshots, 2026-11-04): `.agents/plans/assets/gizmos/` — `camera.png`, `directional.png`, `point.png`, `spot.png`. All gizmos are thin 1-px wireframe lines (the existing overlay line pass, soft depth-tested), no fills.

**Shapes (from `scene.lights`: `nodeIndex`, `position`, `direction`, `range`, cone cosines; hidden lights from the Phase 1 filter are not drawn):**
- **Directional (`directional.png`):** a small square plate at the light's node position, perpendicular to the light direction (side ≈ 0.04 × scene extent), plus one long line from the plate centre along the light direction (length ≈ 0.5 × scene extent, or to the scene bounds).
- **Point (`point.png`):** a wireframe diamond (octahedron: 6 vertices on ±X/±Y/±Z, 12 edges) centred on the light, radius ≈ 0.03 × scene extent. If `range` is set, optionally a faint circle at `range` (only when selected).
- **Spot (`spot.png`):** a cone from the apex at the light position along its direction: a base circle (32 segments) at length L, radius L·tan(outerConeAngle); 4 generator lines from the apex to the circle at 90° steps; the central axis line from the apex toward the base (stopping just short of the base like the reference); a second, fainter circle for the inner cone angle. description:

## TDD execution contract
- The cases below are defined test contracts, not implemented tests or observed failures. Baseline: **not run for this backlog edit**. Use existing suites where they cover the behavior; proposed suite names are destinations, not existing files.
- **Red first:** after prerequisites are available, add the smallest deterministic behavioral test before its production change. Run the focused suite and record test name, command, revision/worktree state, actual failing assertion and log path. A missing API/compiler error may guide initial scaffolding, but establish a compiling behavioral failure before implementation; build/tool/fixture errors are not feature-red evidence. Never use unconditional failures, skip/expected-failure markers, or loosen an oracle to manufacture red.
- **Green, then refactor:** implement only enough to pass that test, run the remaining cases, then refactor with tests green. Blocked leaves define tests now and establish executable red after their prerequisite lands; do not invent placeholder dependencies.
- For already implemented behavior, keep the regression green and, where safe, prove sensitivity using a temporary isolated mutation/reversion of only that behavior. Do not undo another worker's edits or claim retroactive red. Record unavailable red evidence honestly.
- **Completion evidence:** case → test/fixture → observed red (or documented existing-behavior exception) → green, with commands and log paths in the result. Passing tests alone do not prove this contract was followed.

### Defined tests (write before production changes)
1. Command/Shift toggle picks select two distinct nodes with a stable primary; toggling one off preserves the other and updates primary deterministically.
2. Hide/solo/frame and overlay bounds act on the entire set, including a selected ancestor with its descendant without duplicate effects.
3. Hosted sidebar and canvas share the same selection; inspector shows primary and count; plain click replaces selection and background click clears it.

### TDD verification
Focused command: `./scripts/dev.sh test -only-testing:GLTFInspectorTests/MultiSelectionTests` (reuse/extend an existing suite if appropriate; confirm tests are discovered and executed, not zero tests). After green run `./scripts/dev.sh test` including unchanged pixel references. Use hand-computed expectations/independent Khronos output for renderer math, not values copied from the implementation.

For UI assertions prefer deterministic in-process hosted components and background AX selection; visual checks must inspect the actual rendered result. These instructions supersede older generic launch/uitest directions in this description: background only, no focus steal, no `--snapshot`, no leftover Export sheets; XCUITest requires explicit approval for that run. No app launch is required for this backlog edit.

## Executable TDD baseline — 2026-11-04

Selection is still a single NodeID and the pick callback carries one index with no selection modifiers. A set/primary-selection command seam is needed for the toggle/aggregate-action contracts. Existing plain-click tests are not multiselect tests.

Do not label this leaf test-ready until its defined cases compile, execute and fail on behavior. Interface/build errors are not feature-red evidence.

name: Verify from Finder with the signed installed extension
description:
## Why

This is the measurement the whole spike exists for. Everything before it runs in processes that are more permissive than the real one.

## Why Finder specifically

- `qlmanage` **hangs headless on this machine** (`scripts/proof.sh` wraps it in a 12 s `alarm` and treats a timeout as expected). It is not a usable oracle here.
- `qlmanage -x` exercises a different reply path than Finder. `ThumbnailProvider.swift` documents that the `CGContext` reply works under `qlmanage -x` but fails with `QLThumbnailError 102` on the generator path Finder actually uses. A `qlmanage` pass would not be evidence.

Finder, with a real installed and signed build, is the only oracle that counts.

## Approach

```bash
cd .worktrees/web-thumb-spike
./scripts/build.sh                 # installs to /Applications and verifies with pluginkit
defaults write lol.mattias.gltf-inspector.spike WebThumbnail -bool YES
```

Force Finder to regenerate rather than serve a cached icon — a stale cache is the classic false negative here:

```bash
qlmanage -r cache
killall Finder
```

Then copy a few Khronos samples into a fresh folder (new inodes defeat any per-file cache) and open it in icon view:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/thumb-check && cp "TestModels/Khronos samples/BoomBox/BoomBox.glb" \
  "TestModels/Khronos samples/Corset/Corset.glb" \
  "TestModels/Fixture Models/tiny.glb" /tmp/thumb-check/
open /tmp/thumb-check
```

Watch the extension while it runs:

```bash
log stream --style compact --info --predicate 'subsystem == "lol.mattias.gltf-inspector"'
```

Capture the icon-view result with Peekaboo per the `macos-app-testing` skill — **background capture, no `activate`, no focus steal**, `PEEKABOO_CAPTURE_ENGINE=classic`. Per `AGENTS.md`: warn before anything moves focus.

## What to record

Both outcomes are a result. Neither is a failure of the spike.

- **Go:** correct thumbnails in Finder. Record wall-clock time per file from the log, and whether `com.apple.WebKit.WebContent` / `.GPU` appear as children of the extension in Activity Monitor.
- **No-go:** record the exact failure. `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` firing is the expected shape of a sandbox denial. Cross-check with:
  ```bash
  log stream --predicate 'subsystem == "com.apple.sandbox" OR eventMessage CONTAINS "deny"'
  ```
  Capture the literal `deny(1) ...` lines — they name which operation the seatbelt refused, which is what makes the finding actionable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Finder icon view screenshotted with the web path enabled.
- Log excerpt showing which renderer ran, and either per-file timings or the specific failure.
- If it failed: the sandbox denial lines, plus a note on whether an entitlement change fixed it and which one.
- The flag flipped back to `NO` and RealityKit thumbnails confirmed still working, so the machine is not left in a spike state.
result:
## Result: **GO** — with a one-line entitlement change

WebGL renders inside the real, signed, sandboxed `QLThumbnailProvider`, and Finder displays the results.

Verified through `QLThumbnailGenerator.generateBestRepresentation` — the same generator path Finder uses, per the existing comment in `ThumbnailProvider.swift` — and then visually in Finder icon view.

## The blocker, and the fix

Stock entitlements fail. Every request died the same way:

```
Sandbox: ThumbnailExtension(37619) deny(1) mach-issue-extension
  target:com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd
  extension-class:com.apple.webkit.extension.mach
```

The extension cannot issue the mach sandbox extensions WebContent needs, so WebContent dies on launch. Surfaced exactly as instrumented — `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` → `webContentTerminated` → `QLThumbnailError 102`. Four of four files failed.

**Adding `com.apple.security.network.client` alone fixes it.** Isolated by adding it together with `temporary-exception.mach-lookup.global-name` for `launchservicesd` + `lsd.mapdb`, then removing the mach-lookup exceptions and re-testing: still passes. The minimal delta is one boolean.

`WKWebView` spawns a Networking XPC service even when the page makes zero network requests — this page loads only from a custom scheme handler. The `mach-issue-extension` denial still appears in the log afterwards but is no longer fatal.

## Timings (512px, through the real extension)

| File | Total | In page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BoomBox 10 MB | 1807 ms | 773 ms |
| BarramundiFish 12 MB | 1833 ms | 1070 ms |
| Corset 13 MB | 1841 ms | 1081 ms |
| tiny.glb 428 B | 292 ms | 124 ms |

Three large files ran concurrently, so the ~1.8 s figures share extension start-up; `tiny.glb` arrived later into an already-warm process and cost 292 ms.

**This is materially slower than RealityKit**, which produced the same 512px PNGs in **163–235 ms** in-process. Roughly 4–8x on cold work. Not disqualifying for Finder (thumbnails are async and cached), but it is the real cost and belongs in the decision.

## Evidence

- `/tmp/qlgen-BoomBox-27082.png` — WebGL output via the extension: transparent background, cyan emissive PLAY button, correct silver/black PBR.
- `/tmp/finder-icons.png` — Finder icon view, all four thumbnails correct.
- `/tmp/spike-sandbox.txt` — raw denial lines.

The RealityKit render of the same file is visibly different: opaque grey 0.94 background, PLAY button unlit. That difference is what caught the first false positive.

## Two false positives worth recording

Both reported success while the RealityKit path was actually running. Neither was caught by an assertion — only by looking at the image.

1. **`UserDefaults(suiteName:)` is invisible to a sandboxed extension.** It reads preferences from its own container, so `defaults write` on a shared suite never arrives. Flag read `false`, RealityKit ran, thumbnails looked fine.
2. **`homeDirectoryForCurrentUser` returns the container home under the sandbox**, not the real one — so does `NSHomeDirectory()`. The marker-file replacement was looked for in the wrong directory and also read `false`. `getpwuid(getuid())->pw_dir` gives the real home.

## Machine state: an unrelated finding, and what was changed

`lsregister -dump` listed **22 registered copies** of `glTF Inspector.app`, and `pluginkit` was resolving the active thumbnail extension to a stale Xcode DerivedData build from 22 Aug — not `/Applications`. Any previous thumbnail verification on this machine was testing an arbitrary old build.

Unregistered the 20 stale copies (ephemeral DerivedData, XcodeBuildMCP test products, `/tmp` build dirs), ran the spike against a single known registration, then restored: spike build unregistered, `/Applications/glTF Inspector.app` re-registered and now the active provider, marker file removed, `qlmanage -r cache` run, temp folders deleted. Machine is in a cleaner state than before.

Committed as `347c390` on `spike/web-thumbnail`.

name: Camera gizmo: pyramid frustum with up triangle
description:
**Why:** see where each authored camera is, which way is up, and what it frames.

Reference look (user screenshots, 2026-11-04): `.agents/plans/assets/gizmos/` — `camera.png`, `directional.png`, `point.png`, `spot.png`. All gizmos are thin 1-px wireframe lines (the existing overlay line pass, soft depth-tested), no fills.

**Camera shape (`camera.png`):** a pyramid. Apex at the camera node's world position; a rectangle at a display distance in front of it (along the camera's −Z); four edges from the apex to the rectangle corners; plus an **up triangle** sitting on the rectangle's top edge (pointing along the camera's +Y), about 1/3 of the rectangle width, drawn in a distinct colour (blue in the reference) so "up" reads at a glance.
- Rectangle size from the camera's values: perspective → half-height = d·tan(yfov/2), half-width = half-height·aspect (`aspectRatio`, else the canvas aspect); orthographic → a box: rectangle of xmag×ymag at both z = −znear and z = −d with parallel edges instead of a pyramid.
- Display distance d = 0.15 × the scene's largest extent (not zfar, which is usually huge); never smaller than znear.
- Colours: selected camera node = highlight (yellow/orange like the reference, add `DS`-matching constant in `MetalOverlays.swift`), others = muted grey; the up triangle = the axis blue for selected, grey otherwise.

**Scope:** `MetalOverlayOptions` gains `sceneGizmos: Bool`; `overlayVertices` (`Renderer/MetalOverlays.swift`) walks `scene.asset.nodes` with a camera (world matrix like `MetalScene.fileCamera`). `ViewOptions.showsSceneGizmos: Bool = false` ← `ViewState.showsSceneGizmos` + View menu toggle "Show Cameras & Lights" (only when the document has cameras or lights — hide, don't disable). The selected camera node is always drawn even with the toggle off. Skip the camera you are currently looking through (`fileCameraNodeIndex`).

**Done when:** both cameras of `cameras/persp-and-ortho.gltf` show the right shape (pyramid vs box) with the up triangle on top; selecting one turns it highlight-coloured; matches `camera.png` in style.
**Verification:** unit test on `overlayVertices` (segment count; a rectangle corner and the up-triangle apex for a known perspective camera); on-screen screenshot next to `camera.png`; `./scripts/dev.sh test` with references unchanged (gizmos are off by default).

**Spec:** `.agents/plans/2026-11-04-scene-interaction.md` (coverage table + decisions log). Read `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md` first.
**Rules:** work on `main` unless told otherwise; never regenerate pixel references for a default render (`TestModels/References/`); new UI goes through `GLTFInspector/DesignSystem/` components; check UI on screen yourself (`./scripts/dev.sh run <fixture>`, `screencapture`), never ask the user to test.

- The cases below are defined test contracts, not implemented tests or observed failures. Baseline: **not run for this backlog edit**. Use existing suites where they cover the behavior; proposed suite names are destinations, not existing files.
- **Red first:** after prerequisites are available, add the smallest deterministic behavioral test before its production change. Run the focused suite and record test name, command, revision/worktree state, actual failing assertion and log path. A missing API/compiler error may guide initial scaffolding, but establish a compiling behavioral failure before implementation; build/tool/fixture errors are not feature-red evidence. Never use unconditional failures, skip/expected-failure markers, or loosen an oracle to manufacture red.
- **Green, then refactor:** implement only enough to pass that test, run the remaining cases, then refactor with tests green. Blocked leaves define tests now and establish executable red after their prerequisite lands; do not invent placeholder dependencies.
- For already implemented behavior, keep the regression green and, where safe, prove sensitivity using a temporary isolated mutation/reversion of only that behavior. Do not undo another worker's edits or claim retroactive red. Record unavailable red evidence honestly.
- **Completion evidence:** case → test/fixture → observed red (or documented existing-behavior exception) → green, with commands and log paths in the result. Passing tests alone do not prove this contract was followed.

### Defined tests (write before production changes)
1. For a fixed perspective camera assert apex, four display-plane corners using d×tan(yfov/2) and aspect, plus the up-triangle apex in transformed world coordinates.
2. For an orthographic camera assert parallel near/far edges using the documented xmag/ymag semantics; absent aspect uses canvas aspect and d never falls below znear.

name: Strip Quick Look to canvas chrome
description:
## Why

QL today shows full inlined chrome when tapped. Product scope is a light canvas preview. Shared
chrome files can die only after this carve.

## Where the QL chrome actually lives (important)

`PreviewExtension/` does **not** reference `PreviewChromeBar` / `PreviewCycleMenu` /
`PreviewOverlayFacts` directly (grep is clean). QL hosts `PreviewView` → `PreviewScene` with
`sidebar == nil`, and `PreviewScene` itself inlines the chrome (`PreviewChromeBar` at
`PreviewScene.swift:410`, gizmo/facts/playback around it). `vfcn76gm` added a host-bare mode; the
**QL (non-host) branch of `PreviewScene`** is what still draws chrome. So this task edits that QL
branch, not the extension target.

## Scope

- Keep in the QL path: orbit / scroll-dolly / shift-pan (`PreviewInteraction`), bottom-left
  `PreviewOverlayFacts`, and **two** glass buttons — backdrop cycle + auto-rotate — carved from
  `PreviewChromeBar` / `PreviewCycleMenu` + `previewGlassButtonStyle` into a small QL-only chrome
  view.
- Remove everything else from the QL path: the full pills/outliner/view-mode/lighting/floor/presets
  and any tap-to-reveal menu.
- Then delete the remainder of `Shared/PreviewChromeBar.swift` and `Shared/PreviewCycleMenu.swift`.
  `PreviewPlaybackBar` lives inside `PreviewChromeBar.swift`, so playback must already be
  engine-backed on the host (it is, via the seam) and QL does not need a playback bar.
- **Never delete** `Shared/PreviewChrome.swift` (it holds `PreviewInteraction` /
  `PreviewHostingView` — both host and QL need it).
- `ThumbnailExtension`: re-run its tests only; no UI change (it already excludes all UI files).
- Out of scope: host window chrome (already PreviewUI).

## Done when

Finder QL on a `.glb`: model orbits, info bottom-left, the two buttons work, nothing else, no crash.
Host still builds. `ThumbnailExtension` tests pass. Grep: no dangling `PreviewChromeBar` /
`PreviewCycleMenu` references anywhere.

## Handoff

QL chrome view file path; thumbnail test result; confirm both chrome files are deleted.
